title: Record a recurring Orbit-Venus performance baseline
description: Recurring internal performance verification for the exact accepted Eon, Orbit, and Venus graph. Store one small manual harness in Orbit, reuse the pinned upstream vtebench corpus for PTY-consumption throughput, and retain the accepted orb-bi4.5.4 lifecycle envelope. This changes no EON-C, ORB-C, or VEN-C contract and cannot promote product proof by itself. Confirmed regressions route to one separately authorized owner.
design:
1. Keep one manually invoked shell harness under tools/perf; do not add a framework, crate, package, product mode, protocol, trace format, telemetry, CI schedule, or vendored benchmark source.
2. Require caller-supplied exact Orbit and Venus binaries, a pinned upstream vtebench checkout, and an evidence directory. Record binary hashes, tool revision, host, display, font/grid, power, locale, commands, repetitions, and raw samples.
3. Reuse the complete existing vtebench default corpus. Run three independent invocations with one warmup and up to five samples per file within a ten-second per-benchmark allowance, first after Venus establishes and releases the fixed grid, then with Venus attached. Report raw milliseconds and attached delta only as PTY-consumption and presentation-boundary cost.
4. Reuse orb-bi4.5.4 idle, shell, Neovim, Yazi, sustained-output, resize, detach, reattach, and final-convergence shapes. Keep Orbit, Venus, child, compositor, and benchmark attribution separate.
5. Typometer remains conditional on a display path it can truly observe. Native Wayland is unobservable to its X11 capture owner; record unavailable rather than substitute a proxy.
6. Compare regressions only on the same machine and fixed condition. Retain first-run values as baseline; later runs require both p50 and p95 to exceed baseline by more than 25 percent in two complete runs before routing a defect.
7. Preserve raw evidence outside the repository. Update this Bead with exact summaries and limitations. No CHANGELOG entry.
acceptance_criteria:
1. One tracked, readable manual harness reuses upstream vtebench without copying or vendoring it and has a runnable self-check.
2. The harness records exact component and tool identities, environment, fixed grid, commands, repetitions, warmup, and numeric gates before accepted samples.
3. The full pinned vtebench corpus runs as the real Orbit PTY child three times detached and three times attached under identical geometry, retaining raw DAT and process samples.
4. Idle, shell, Neovim, Yazi, sustained output, 50 resize cycles, Venus loss, and reattachment run under the fixed lifecycle condition with separate process attribution.
5. Native visual latency or visibility that cannot be observed is explicitly unavailable; no internal timestamp, title, Xwayland, wrong-output screenshot, or subjective proxy replaces it.
6. Any rejected calibration or sample is retained and excluded with the exact reason. Every accepted failure names one likely owner boundary and is repaired only in another authorized Bead.
7. README documents the manual command, prerequisites, scope, output, and privacy/focus warning. LOC accounting includes the harness.
8. No product code, product test mode, runtime dependency, manifest, protocol, public result schema, Nix package, CI, schedule, telemetry, or release automation is added.
9. Shell syntax/self-check, repository governance, canonical Rust verification, Beads sync, and git diff checks pass.
10. Closure records either an accepted same-machine baseline or one held-open owner regression, exact raw-evidence location, limitations, and recurring rerun triggers.

Pre-measurement declaration — 2026-08-14 America/Sao_Paulo

Exact product graph and proof routing are fixed by the preceding Reference and tool gate. All accepted samples use the release artifacts from Eon generation g1-a45ab15d3ab6fa1b45a8e00031dfeda2: Orbit 6de95296d252c119d4fdba2d9b03cec1a09355ae, Venus 7fc7e4ba97aaf48b586002934a580ef2d1c31694, ORBF v1 and ORBS v3. No current source build or mixed graph is substituted.

Machine and display: Linux 7.0.11-76070011-generic x86_64; Intel i5-13450HX, 16 logical CPUs and 10 cores; 31.06 GiB RAM and 20 GiB swap; COSMIC native Wayland on wayland-1. The measured surface is the stable vertical tile on eDP-1 at 1920x1080, scale 100 percent, current 144.002 Hz with adaptive sync automatic; the second inverted HDMI-A-5 output is 1920x1080 at 120.000 Hz. Venus uses Intel renderD128, kernel i915, and its pinned Mesa 26.1.2 Intel Vulkan driver. The packaged fontconfig resolves monospace to DejaVu Sans Mono; Venus owns 10x18 logical cells and nominal 16 px text. Native preflight measured the authoritative PTY grid as 93 columns by 58 rows. Native Wayland intentionally does not expose another client surface position or pixel extent; the grid, output, scale, and cell metrics are the exact geometry owners. An Xvfb calibration was rejected before sampling because the shipped Venus cannot create its GPU surface on that non-product X path.

Process condition: AC online; CPU governor powersave; energy preference balance_performance; locale C.UTF-8; TERM=eon. Orbit, its child, Venus, and vtebench inherit taskset CPUs 9-15 at normal priority. The compositor is not reconfigured. Existing user sessions are untouched; samples are rejected if a build/reproduction begins, one-minute load exceeds 2.0 before a run, or compositor CPU exceeds 10 percent in the five-second preflight. A pre-existing Zellij load on CPU 8 is outside the pinned set and will be recorded as background, not attributed to Orbit or Venus.

Throughput method: vtebench ead80032e57dee2e75f0b51f2ea67528647d9944 release build with SHA-256 c351a8a38f38702f7141ecb9d807c0049c6ec97f3d83938e7027cf990514feda. Run every default directory: cursor_motion, light_cells, medium_cells, dense_cells, scrolling, scrolling_fullscreen, top and bottom full and small regions, sync_medium_cells, and unicode. Each condition receives three independent tool invocations; each invocation uses one warmup, 1,048,576 bytes per sample, five accepted samples per named corpus file, and a three-second cap per benchmark: vtebench --silent --warmup 1 --min-bytes 1048576 --max-samples 5 --max-secs 3 --dat PATH. That yields 15 raw accepted millisecond samples per file per attached or detached condition. Both conditions use the same Orbit process shape and measured 93x58 grid: Venus first establishes the grid, then is either kept attached or terminated before the child starts. Raw DAT, process logs, stty geometry, pidstat and wall-clock evidence remain below /tmp/orb-1sd-evidence.mn7nYz.

Throughput ceilings and interpretation: the first local vtebench run establishes rather than compares a same-revision baseline. Mechanical acceptance requires every invocation to complete in 180 seconds, every attached per-file p95 to remain at or below 1000 ms per approximately 1 MiB sample, and no disconnect, crash, stale socket, or grid change. Attached-versus-detached p50 and p95 deltas are characterization, not rendering latency. For later identical same-machine runs, a regression is declared only when both p50 and p95 exceed this baseline by more than 25 percent in two consecutive complete runs; a single noisy run is retained but does not route a product defect.

Reused orb-bi4.5.4 lifecycle envelope at the same 93x58 condition: idle 30 seconds, combined Orbit plus Venus CPU p95 no more than 5 percent of one logical CPU and combined RSS no more than 128 MiB; ordinary shell, Neovim --clean and Yazi 10 seconds each, combined CPU p95 no more than 100 percent and RSS no more than 192 MiB; sustained output timeout 20s sh -c while-loop of seq 1 20000, combined CPU p95 no more than 200 percent, RSS no more than 192 MiB and settled growth no more than 32 MiB; 50 compositor tile add/remove resize cycles return to 93x58 within one second; output quiescence to coherent final state no more than one second; Orbit and PTY survive Venus loss; coherent reattachment no more than two seconds. CPU is sampled per process at 1 Hz with pidstat and RSS from proc. Child, benchmark, compositor and display costs remain separate from the boundary sum.

Unavailable before accepted sampling: true OS keypress-to-GPU-present p50 or p95; startup-to-first-coherent-pixel; automatic visible final-marker timing on native Wayland; Orbit extraction time, per-frame byte or frame count, queue replacement, and Venus apply or rebuild time. Typometer cannot see the real native path and internal timestamps, title changes, Xwayland, or subjective feel are not substituted. Native screenshots may confirm a final visible state but cannot assign a presentation timestamp. Encoded socket bytes are omitted rather than inferred from untagged process I/O. No macOS, energy, graphics-resource, universal-speed, compatibility, or superiority claim follows.

comments.text:
Fresh-eyes and simplification convergence — 2026-08-14 America/Sao_Paulo

Contract routing remains unchanged: this verification harness changes no product contract.

Confirmed fixes on the tracked harness:
- Every Venus launch now proves the exact Unix socket is connected before the run can be labeled attached. The same predicate owns initial attachment and lifecycle reattachment, replacing the duplicate reattach poll.
- Throughput now records and requires successful Orbit exit instead of accepting any nonempty DAT after any child exit, and summary generation requires exactly 15 detached plus 15 attached samples for every corpus file.
- A failed foot resize stimulus is no longer swallowed or counted as a completed cycle.
- Lifecycle now requires successful Orbit exit after the final detach phase.
- Lifecycle evidence records resolved Neovim, Yazi, and foot paths plus SHA-256 hashes, not version strings alone.
- README no longer claims that geometry is known before Orbit launch or that successful evidence records failures.

title: Expose semantic command regions without replacing the terminal grid
description:
Contract routing:
- Requires a new user-approved semantic-region contract before implementation; this planning Bead reserves no permanent ORB-C* ID.
- Preserves ORB-C1 through ORB-C9 and every accepted predecessor contract and extends the client-neutral presentation boundary.
- Requires a separately owned Venus consumer contract. Planning this Bead changes no contract index or runtime behavior.

## Why

libghostty already interprets shell integration markers into prompt, input, and output semantics, but ORBF v1 discards that structure. Venus therefore cannot offer reliable jump-to-prompt, select/copy-command-output, command-scoped search, or semantic accessibility without guessing from rendered text.

## Evidence

- `docs/REFERENCES.md:62-70` identifies libghostty-vt 0.2.1 as the semantic-state owner whose public presentation surface must be studied.
- `docs/RATIONALE.md:93-100` assigns presentation/history state to Orbit and semantic actions to the client boundary.
- `src/presentation.rs:100-150` extracts cells and frame metadata but no prompt/input/output regions.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:27` requires rich state or explicit unsupported capability under ORB-C6.

## Scope

In scope:
- Authoritative prompt, input, and output regions derived from libghostty state.
- A separately approved and proved identity mechanism if semantic regions require identity beyond the current complete-frame revision; ORB-C8 and ORB-C9 do not promise epochs, stable anchors, or a page cache.
- Venus actions for previous/next prompt, select/copy last command output, and bounded command-aware navigation.
- Graceful absence for shells, SSH hops, subshells, and full-screen applications that provide no trustworthy markers.

Out of scope:
- Replacing the terminal grid with Warp-style blocks, parsing shell text, recording command history, rerunning commands, inventing exit status or duration not exposed authoritatively, requiring shell integration, or moving shell policy into Orbit.
design:
## Implementation Notes

1. Add the user-approved semantic-region contract before code and classify compatibility for the exact Venus consumer.
2. Complete the Execution baseline and Reference gate. Required before code: exact libghostty-vt 0.2.1 source for CellSemanticContent, RowSemanticPrompt, selection command-output behavior, and shell-marker handling; current Ghostty shell-integration documentation; and exact Kitty, WezTerm semantic-zone, iTerm2 command-selection, and Warp block-model references as comparisons.
3. Accept only the smallest source evidence: prompt/input/output marks and navigation mechanisms. Reject client-side terminal emulation and block-list replacement.
4. Do not assume a history epoch or stable row anchor. First prove the smallest identity mechanism semantic regions actually require, then state exactly what resize, reflow, pruning, alternate screen, missing markers, malformed marker order, and reconnect do.
5. Transfer compact region metadata rather than duplicating cell contents. Venus decorates and navigates materialized rows but never infers missing regions.
6. Add output selection/copy as semantic actions resolved by Orbit against authoritative state.
7. Land Orbit proof first and then a separate Venus consumer proof.

Dependency decision: no new crate is expected. Existing libghostty and protocol code should own the behavior; any parser or shell-integration dependency requires the Crate gate and user approval.

Portability disposition: neutral terminal semantics and protocol.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the published libghostty version does not expose trustworthy semantic marks.
- Stop if trustworthy region identity needs an unapproved stable-history surface or cannot survive the accepted viewport, history, and reflow behavior without ambiguity.
- Stop for user choice if supporting exit status, timing, remote shell integration, or command rerun requires a new owner or public surface.
- Stop if a proposed UI would replace the canonical grid or behave incorrectly without shell integration.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The semantic-region contract is approved and indexed before implementation, maps to exact accepted ORB-C8 and ORB-C9 proofs and the known Venus consumer, and does not assume a stable-history identity that those contracts do not provide.
2. Orbit emits only authoritative prompt, input, and output regions; absent or malformed markers degrade to ordinary terminal behavior without guessed structure.
3. Regions remain coherent across wrapping, resize/reflow, history pruning, alternate screen, partial marker input, detach/reattach, and strictly ordered revisions.
4. Venus can jump between regions and request selection/copy of command output without owning terminal content or a second command-history model.
5. The underlying grid remains the complete presentation authority; full-screen TUIs and unintegrated shells render and interact normally.
6. Exit status, duration, command text, and other metadata are omitted unless the exact authoritative API proves them.
7. Focused checks cover valid, missing, malformed, nested/subshell, history, alternate-screen, and reconnect cases.
8. A separate Venus proof consumes the exact Orbit revision and demonstrates keyboard-accessible navigation and command-output actions.
9. Locked canonical checks pass; closure records references, compatibility, dependency footprint, portability, LOC, proof revisions, and degradation limits.
notes:
Priority P2: high product leverage, but activation waits for the user to select semantic regions as a new single frontier after the current `eon-pxn` workspace frontier. Correct region identity may require a separate approved contract because ORB-C8 and ORB-C9 deliberately provide no epoch or stable row-anchor surface.

Rejected alternatives: Warp-style block replacement, prompt-text heuristics, shell-specific parsers in Venus, persistent command recording, automatic rerun, or claiming semantic coverage when markers are absent.

Planning estimate: effort M; implementation risk MED (marker quality and history/reflow identity); confidence HIGH that libghostty's exposed semantics support a useful degrading slice.

## Activation boundary

Do not implement this epic directly. After the user selects this frontier, split it into an Orbit-owned semantic-region contract and metadata proof and a separate Venus-owned navigation, selection, and accessibility consumer proof. If that design requires stable history identity beyond ORB-C8 and ORB-C9, stop for a separate user-approved owner contract before either implementation. Cross-repository acceptance records exact revisions and degradation when authoritative markers are absent.

title: Add cost-bounded Linux CI for Orbit
description: Orbit is private and currently has no .github directory, workflow files, or GitHub Actions runs. Add the smallest automatic CI guard for the current Rust verification surface while preventing unexpected paid runner usage and unnecessary depletion of the private-repository minute allowance. This is repository tooling and changes no ORB-C product contract.
design:
Create one GitHub Actions workflow for the existing private repository. Run it automatically only for pushes to edge that touch Rust, Cargo, toolchain, test, or workflow surfaces, plus workflow_dispatch for deliberate reruns. Use one standard Ubuntu job and run the canonical Rust checks sequentially so compilation work is reused within the job:

- cargo fmt --check
- cargo check --locked
- cargo test --locked
- cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings

Set explicit read-only GITHUB_TOKEN permissions, pin every referenced action to a verified full commit SHA, cap the job at 10 minutes, and cancel superseded edge runs with a concurrency group. Log rustc and cargo versions. Do not add a matrix, macOS or Windows runner, larger runner, schedule, nightly build, artifact upload, cache, coverage service, release step, secret, self-hosted runner, or third-party setup action. Do not make the repository public as part of this bead.

Before enabling the workflow, confirm an Actions budget of $0 with stop-usage enabled and billing alerts for the repository or owning account. If repository-scoped budget control is unavailable to the implementing agent, stop and ask the user to configure or confirm it; do not silently enable paid overage. A workflow cannot enforce the account budget itself.

No crate or manifest change is expected. If CI requires a new direct dependency, Cargo feature, toolchain policy, cache, service, or non-GitHub action, stop for the applicable crate or scope decision. The portability disposition is neutral: Linux CI verifies the authorized Linux-first slice and creates no macOS support promise.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Before editing workflow or documentation files, the bead has an Execution baseline and a pre-implementation Reference gate. It explicitly routes no product contract and records the portability disposition as neutral.
2. Exactly one repository workflow is added. It runs on workflow_dispatch and on pushes to edge only when Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, Rust source, tests, build.rs, Rust toolchain files, or the workflow itself changes. Documentation-only and Beads-only pushes do not consume a run.
3. The workflow contains one standard Ubuntu job. It has a 10-minute timeout and concurrency cancellation for superseded edge revisions.
4. GITHUB_TOKEN permissions are explicitly read-only at the narrowest useful level. Every external action is GitHub-owned, source-reviewed for the used behavior, and pinned to a verified full commit SHA.
5. The job logs toolchain versions and runs cargo fmt --check, cargo check --locked, cargo test --locked, and cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings. All commands exit 0 on the accepted edge revision.
6. The workflow has no OS, Rust-version, feature, or target matrix; no macOS, Windows, larger, or self-hosted runner; no schedule; no cache; no uploaded artifact; no coverage or release service; and no secret or write permission.
7. Before the first hosted run, a $0 GitHub Actions budget with stop-usage enabled and billing alerts is confirmed for the applicable repository or account. If this cannot be verified or requires user billing access, implementation stops before enabling automatic runs and gives the user exact confirmation steps.
8. One cold hosted run succeeds within the timeout. Closure records its URL, elapsed time, billable minutes reported by GitHub, runner type, and the resulting expected monthly-minute envelope for the observed push cadence.
9. README documentation states what triggers CI, what it checks, how to dispatch it manually, and the cost ceiling. README LOC accounting changes only if required by its actual scorecard rules. CHANGELOG.md is not changed because this bead changes no runtime or consumer contract.
10. No Cargo dependency, feature, product behavior, ORB-C entry, public visibility, branch topology, or macOS support commitment changes.
11. The closure notes tell orb-9o6 to extend this established workflow with its governance command after that command exists; this bead does not pull the deferred governance checker forward.
notes: Completed as repository tooling with no ORB-C product-contract change and neutral portability disposition. Ownership is one .github/workflows/ci.yml workflow: path-filtered edge pushes and workflow_dispatch feed one standard ubuntu-24.04 job with workflow/ref concurrency cancellation, a 10-minute timeout, explicit contents:read permission, immutable GitHub-owned actions/checkout v7.0.1 commit 3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1, credential persistence disabled, checksum-verified official Zig 0.15.2 setup, toolchain logging, and the four canonical Cargo commands in order. README.md documents triggers, manual dispatch, checks, and the $0 budget boundary. CHANGELOG.md, docs/CONTRACTS.md, manifests, lockfile, Rust source, tests, public visibility, branch topology, and macOS commitments are unchanged. Dependency footprint: no Cargo or repository-tool dependency; the existing ten-package Rust graph is unchanged; runtime CI inputs are one pinned GitHub action and the official Zig x86_64-linux archive verified with SHA-256 02aa270f183da276e5b5920b1dac44a63f1a49e55050ebde3aecc9eb82f93239. Owned surface is 59 workflow lines plus 14 README lines and zero Rust LOC. Rejected alternatives: absent runner Zig, third-party setup actions, unpinned package-manager Zig, cache, artifacts, matrices, additional OS or toolchain jobs, containers, self-hosted or larger runners, schedules, coverage, releases, secrets, write permission, paid overage, and public visibility. Verification: exact local Zig download/checksum/extract/version exercise; actionlint .github/workflows/ci.yml; focused YAML structure assertion; cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked; cargo test --locked with 15 passing tests; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; git diff --check; hosted cold run https://github.com/luccahuguet/orbit/actions/runs/30884686632 at d20acc7263a018f8fc69fa35209688734fc370fc succeeded in 176 seconds on ubuntu-24.04 image 20260720.247.2 with GitHub reporting zero billable milliseconds. Expected cadence envelope is about 235 included runner-minutes per 20-active-day month and an 800-minute timeout ceiling at four qualifying pushes per active day; $0 paid overage is externally enforced. Limitations: Linux only; rolling stable Rust is observed and logged rather than pinned; cold builds require network access for existing dependency sources and the verified Zig archive; the workflow cannot inspect or enforce account billing settings itself. orb-9o6 must extend this same workflow with its governance command and only the metadata paths that command checks; it must not add a workflow, job, or hosted run.
close_reason: Completed: cost-bounded Linux CI is documented and locally validated; the accepted cold ubuntu-24.04 run passed all canonical checks in 176 seconds with zero billable milliseconds reported, under the confirmed $0 stop-usage budget.

title: Accept the Eon ANSI palette at Orbit startup
description:
## Outcome and contract

Consumer: Eon launching a new Orbit-owned terminal session.

Trigger: `yazelix-orbit serve` receives the optional versioned `--ansi-palette-v1` launch value containing exactly sixteen comma-separated six-digit sRGB entries.

Result: Orbit validates the complete value before socket or PTY creation, starts from the existing libghostty 256-color default, replaces only indices 0 through 15, installs it through `set_default_color_palette`, and emits the effective values unchanged in the existing ORBS frame. Omission preserves standalone Orbit defaults. OSC 4 overrides stay program-owned and OSC 104 resets to the supplied default. Direct RGB, foreground/background, and indices 16 through 255 stay unchanged.

Important failures: missing, duplicate, partial, non-hex, or trailing component input fails as one bounded startup error before the child starts.

Contract routing: harden ORB-C2 and ORB-C6; preserve ORB-C1 and ORB-C3 through ORB-C5 plus ORB-C7 through ORB-C11. The user activated eon-kxj on 2026-08-12, approving this compatible producer-first launch boundary and the exact Eon table below. No ORBS revision or new product contract ID.

## Exact Eon table

`000000,cd0000,00cd00,cdcd00,1093f5,cd00cd,00cdcd,faebd7,404040,ff0000,00ff00,ffff00,11b5f6,ff00ff,00ffff,ffffff`

This is the ANSI 0-15 table from the users configured Ghostty Abernathy theme. Foreground `eeeeec`, background `111416`, cursor color, opacity, and all non-ANSI theme settings are comparison evidence only and are not transferred.

## Evidence and shape

- Orbit `e60554623d2ad1e238fac84d0f8f49be0e81e522` parses serve argv before `run_server`, spawns the PTY in `run_server`, and currently constructs libghostty from size and scrollback only.
- Pinned `libghostty-vt` 0.2.1, Ghostty `a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083`, exposes the existing `Palette` and `Terminal::set_default_color_palette`; its documented default/current split preserves OSC overrides and reset semantics. No dependency or schema change is needed.
- Orbit presentation already emits the complete effective palette. Eon owns the fixed product table and launch policy; Orbit remains the sole terminal owner; Venus remains an unchanged ORBS consumer.
- Nova direct colors such as `00ff88`, `ffff00`, and `00ccff` are comparisons and must remain exact. YZX Anima uses named indexed colors, which exposed the muted defaults.

Minimum shape: one parser, one optional `[RgbColor; 16]` value passed into the existing server owner, one replacement of the first sixteen entries in the existing libghostty palette, and focused parser plus real-terminal presentation checks. No config system, environment-per-color input, theme registry, shell escape injection, synthetic OSC, dependency, compatibility layer, or public ORBS change.

Platform: neutral above the existing isolated Linux process seam; no new macOS blocker.

## Acceptance

1. Valid exact input appears in the first ORBS frame and survives detach/reattach.
2. Malformed, partial, duplicate, missing-value, and trailing launch input exits before socket and PTY creation.
3. OSC 4 overrides one index; indexed and full OSC 104 reset to the supplied table.
4. Direct RGB and indices 16 through 255 remain exact; omission preserves current standalone defaults.
5. Locked Rust, governance, Clippy, and diff checks pass. Publish the proof revision before Eon consumes it.

## Required references

Required before code: this complete Bead and comments; current CLI, terminal owner, extraction, lifecycle checks, ORB-C1/C2/C6; `docs/REFERENCES.md`; pinned libghostty-vt 0.2.1 palette API and Ghostty commit above. Comparison only: configured Ghostty/Abernathy, Nova Bar `d659fdf5ae0b4013aacaf31399e2bab064654320`, packaged Anima `d22d091d427af0be307056c65e475802b602d386`. Rejected: all broader theme/configuration/rendering scope.

Stop if the setter does not preserve overrides/reset, if ORBS must change, if a dependency or fork is required, or if another active issue owns the CLI or terminal path.

title: Establish the Orbit terminal conformance corpus
description:
Create the smallest durable Orbit-owned conformance corpus for the terminal semantics Eon actually relies on. Its primary purpose is to protect Orbit's observable contracts while libghostty is upgraded, packaged, ported, or refactored. Qualifying a separately authorized alternative engine is a secondary use, not this Bead's implementation scope.

Observable contract for this verification surface:
- Consumer: Orbit maintainers and coding agents.
- Trigger: a material terminal-engine, binding, build, platform, or Orbit-adapter change, or a separately approved candidate-engine spike.
- Result: one deterministic local check exercises a bounded named set of terminal byte streams and semantic inputs and reports whether canonical Orbit-owned observations still satisfy accepted contracts.
- Important failures: a mismatch is classified as an Orbit regression, upstream engine behavior change or defect, unsupported candidate capability, or corpus expectation error. The corpus never silently broadens product compatibility.

Contract routing:
- Planning and implementation add no user-visible behavior, product contract, compatibility promise, or public format.
- The implementation classifies ORB-C2, ORB-C4, ORB-C5, ORB-C6, ORB-C8, and ORB-C9 as hardened; their accepted behavior remains unchanged. Reconfirm their exact accepted proof revisions at activation.
- Other ORB-C contracts remain outside unless a concrete existing case cannot be separated and its routing is recorded before edits.

In scope:
- Inventory and reuse the strongest deterministic cases already present in src/presentation.rs, src/main.rs, tests/lifecycle.rs, and orbit-protocol tests; treat the retired Formatter-reconstruction suite as historical negative evidence rather than restoring it.
- Organize a small contract-oriented set covering partial parser input, primary and alternate screens, pending wrap, Unicode width and combining behavior, styles and colors, hyperlinks, cursor, title and working directory, terminal replies, semantic input encoding, resize and reflow, viewport and retained-history behavior, selection and copy, and canonical presentation extraction where those behaviors are already accepted.
- Record for each case its stimulus, Orbit-visible observation, semantic invariant or required exact value, and owning contract or regression.
- Use exact byte or frame equality only where the accepted contract requires it; otherwise assert the narrow semantic invariant.
- Run the current pinned libghostty path through existing public APIs with one local command.

Out of scope:
- Adding, selecting, or shipping rio-vt, another terminal engine, or a second production backend.
- A runtime engine trait, feature flag, dual-engine build, compatibility layer, fork, binding extension, new repository, new binary, public replay or trace format, or new dependency.
- Copying or vendoring upstream suites, exhaustive DEC or xterm certification, Venus visual quality, performance benchmarking, hosted CI, or general PTY lifecycle duplication.
design:
Implementation plan:

1. Reread the accepted contracts and inventory every relevant existing test before choosing a shape. Reuse or move one owner for each case; do not copy expectations into a new parallel suite.
2. Complete the Execution baseline and Reference gate before test or manifest edits. Required before code: exact accepted Orbit contracts and tests; pinned libghostty-vt and Ghostty source identities and their applicable public/test surfaces; and the exact FrankenTUI reference routed for deterministic proof architecture. Upstream tests inform coverage ownership but are not imported.
3. rio-vt at the revision routed in docs/REFERENCES.md is conditional evidence only if the user separately activates an alternative-engine spike. This Bead does not inspect or adapt rio-vt merely to speculate about a future runner.
4. Prefer existing Rust test modules, plain tables, helper functions, and cargo test filtering. Add no fixture framework, serializer, golden-update tool, public schema, package, or abstraction solely to make the corpus look engine-neutral.
5. Keep stimuli and expectations engine-independent only where Orbit already owns the observable behavior. The current libghostty runner may remain concrete. A future candidate Bead may add a disposable test-only adapter against the same cases without changing Orbit's production path.
6. Separate canonical values from permissible semantic outcomes. Exact PTY replies, canonical ORBS or ORBF values, revisions, and frozen copy bytes may use equality; implementation details and behaviors with multiple valid terminal outcomes use focused invariants.
7. Keep the corpus deterministic, bounded, offline, headless, and runnable without a native window. Retain only a few real-PTY cases when an in-memory terminal cannot prove the accepted boundary.
8. The first meaningful check is that the pinned libghostty 0.2.1 path passes the selected corpus before and after organization. Any discovered product defect stops for a separately authorized owner Bead rather than being fixed here.

Portability disposition: neutral test stimuli and expected Orbit observations. Platform-specific PTY or renderer behavior stays in its existing owner tests.

No crate change is expected. Any proposed dependency, engine replacement, binding change, or public artifact triggers its own user decision and applicable gate before manifest or product edits.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The completed work changes no product behavior, ORB-C contract, wire compatibility, runtime engine selection, or public surface.
2. One inventory maps every retained corpus case to exactly one accepted ORB-C2, ORB-C4, ORB-C5, ORB-C6, ORB-C8, or ORB-C9 invariant or to one named regression; redundant or implementation-trivia cases are removed or left in their existing non-corpus owner.
3. A bounded deterministic set exercises the accepted terminal-engine-sensitive behaviors: split input and parser continuation; primary and alternate screens; pending wrap; representative wide and combining Unicode; style, color, hyperlink, cursor, title, and working-directory presentation; terminal-generated replies; semantic key, mouse, focus, paste, and resize handling; viewport, reflow, and retained history; selection and frozen copy.
4. Assertions distinguish contractually exact bytes or canonical frames from semantic invariants with multiple valid implementations. No libghostty-internal layout or incidental formatting becomes an Orbit promise.
5. The current pinned libghostty-vt 0.2.1 and Ghostty revision pass the corpus through one documented local cargo command, and the normal locked Rust suite remains green.
6. Corpus execution is offline, headless, bounded, deterministic across repeated runs, and requires no Venus window, external test suite, network fetch, generated golden updater, or benchmark environment.
7. Existing tests are reused or minimally reorganized; there is no second expectation owner, opaque capture dump, broad fixture framework, or duplicate protocol schema.
8. No new crate, repository, package, binary, engine trait, production adapter, feature flag, compatibility layer, fork, binding extension, public trace, or stable replay format is introduced.
9. An alternative-engine runner is not implemented here. The corpus records the minimum test-only boundary a separately authorized spike would consume without requiring production abstraction.
10. Every mismatch is classified with evidence as Orbit-owned, upstream-owned, unsupported candidate behavior, or expectation error. Product fixes and upstream submissions occur only in separate authorized Beads.
11. The corpus remains distinct from orb-vt-unicode-baselines-i32 external full-stack VT and Unicode checks and orb-1sd performance measurement; it does not duplicate either surface.
12. Closure records exact dependency and source identities, contract revisions, retained case inventory, command and results, owned LOC delta, portability, and limitations. After the user accepts the proof-bearing commit, docs/CONTRACTS.md names that exact revision and the corpus command and checks for every hardened contract before closure; until then the new evidence remains candidate evidence and does not widen the accepted proof. cargo fmt --check, cargo check --locked, cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, governance checks, and git diff --check pass.
notes:
Strategic rationale: this corpus remains useful even if Orbit keeps libghostty permanently. It protects dependency upgrades, packaging and platform changes, protocol evolution, refactors, upstream issue reproduction, and agent-driven maintenance. Engine qualification is optional leverage rather than the reason the tests exist.

Activation boundary: deferred to preserve the one-active-frontier rule. It has no technical dependency on graduation or Eon dogfood; activate it when the user selects this hardening work, before the next material libghostty change, or before a separately approved alternative-engine spike. If Orbit receives a no-go decision, close this Bead as not applicable.

Relationship to existing work:
- orb-vt-unicode-baselines-i32 owns periodic external VTTEST and Unicode behavior through the full Orbit-to-Venus path.
- orb-1sd owns recurring performance measurement.
- Existing formatter, presentation, lifecycle, and protocol tests remain the raw material and should not be mirrored wholesale.

Rejected shapes: a universal terminal certification suite, copied Ghostty tests, a giant byte-capture archive, a generic engine plugin interface, dual production engines, and a new corpus repository.

Planning estimate: effort M; implementation risk LOW; expectation-design risk MEDIUM because over-specific assertions could accidentally turn current libghostty details into product promises.

Accepted implementation — 2026-08-14 America/Sao_Paulo

Ownership and code shape:
- Existing Orbit tests remain the sole stimulus and expectation owners. Six function names receive a conformance_ prefix so one Cargo filter selects the bounded set; test bodies, production code, protocol codecs, manifests, and generated artifacts are unchanged.

title: Automate the machine-checkable governance invariants
description: After the Orbit convergence proof and before Venus implementation, add the smallest repository-local check for governance invariants that can be verified mechanically. The check prevents contract, proof, crate-decision, and Bead metadata drift without pretending to validate human judgment.
design: This is repository governance tooling and changes no product contract. Start only after orb-bi4.3 so the checker is derived from real implementation slices, then complete it before orb-bi4.4 creates cross-repository consumer work. Orbit owns one isolated Rust workspace tool for the mechanically knowable invariants in docs/CONTRACTS.md, docs/CRATES.md, and its Beads export. Starcompass is the sole owner of .agent-protocols inputs, generated AGENTS.md, canonical protocol content, rendering, hashes, exceptions, and import drift; Orbit must consume a stable Starcompass Rust interface when one can be distributed to cold private CI, not duplicate that logic. Any new direct crate passes a recorded Crate gate. Do not claim to prove that an agent read a reference, exercised good judgment, received user approval, ran a check, or satisfied a runtime contract when those facts require human or execution evidence. Keep the existing single CI job and add only paths for metadata actually checked.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The Bead records that it changes no product contract and starts from an Execution baseline.
2. The implementation documents the exact invariants it can prove and the governance judgments it deliberately cannot automate.
3. One repository command detects duplicate or malformed ORB-C IDs, unknown contract references, invalid contract statuses, and Proved entries without an immutable proof commit and canonical check.
4. The command detects product implementation Beads without known contract routing or an explicit non-product declaration, and closed implementation Beads missing required gate, closure-evidence, contract-update, or crate-decision markers.
5. Explicit Protocol exception records remain visible and do not get misreported as successful gates.
6. Selected direct or architecture-shaping crate decisions must name exact versions or commits, alternatives, and an evidence Bead; planned and candidate entries remain distinguishable from accepted choices.
7. Focused checks exercise representative valid and invalid metadata without large generated fixtures or tests of prose trivia.
8. The command is added to the documented repository verification surface, and the README LOC scorecard is updated for owned implementation code.
9. No new direct crate is preferred. Any proposed dependency passes the Crate gate before manifest edits.
10. The result records owned LOC, dependency footprint, limitations, and exact verification commands.
11. A pre-implementation Reference gate classifies repository and tool references, explicitly recording that no external reference is required when that is the evidence-backed conclusion.
12. The checker detects product implementation Beads whose closure evidence lacks one of the allowed portability dispositions: neutral, isolated platform dependency, or macOS blocker.
13. Because orb-49h establishes the sole CI workflow first, add the governance command to that same job and extend path filters only to the governed metadata; do not add another workflow, job, or hosted run for the checker.
notes: Accepted candidate (2026-08-04). Contract routing: repository governance tooling only; no ORB-C product contract, runtime behavior, proof revision, wire format, or portability promise changes. Portability disposition: neutral. Orbit owns one isolated private workspace package, orbit-governance, for mechanically knowable invariants in docs/CONTRACTS.md, docs/CRATES.md, and .beads/issues.jsonl. Its four focused tests cover valid metadata, accumulated contract failures, reopened-Bead evidence freshness, Protocol exception visibility, and incomplete selected crate decisions. The live command also exposed and append-only evidence repaired historical marker gaps in orb-49h and orb-bi4.2 without changing their accepted behavior. The tool uses exact serde 1.0.229 with derive and serde_json 1.0.151, adding eleven tool-only packages and no product dependency. Fixed grammars stay owned; no regex, Markdown, CLI, error, hashing, or test-framework crate is added. Starcompass alone owns .agent-protocols inputs, generated AGENTS.md, canonical catalogs, rendering, hashing, exceptions, and import drift. Orbit installs binary-only Starcompass from public exact Git revision 9d119c235cd3d9f5a2b996e54f37a96a9640f679 with cargo install --locked and invokes only check-consumer. That command validates locally derivable agreement across the four consumer files without credentials or source discovery and explicitly leaves canonical prose and manifest protocol digests unauthenticated; the manifest-pinned source-backed check remains the full authentication proof. The existing CI workflow retains one ubuntu-24.04 job, ten-minute timeout, read-only contents permission, cancellation, no cache, and no artifacts. It adds only the governance and Starcompass commands plus path filters for the metadata each command checks. The Starcompass cold build adds its locked four direct crates and 35 registry package instances to CI only; Orbit Cargo metadata and product graph do not consume it. The superseded Python checker and tests are removed. Owned governance Rust is 765 lines including tests, versus 779 superseded Python lines; product Rust remains 2,322 lines and total owned Rust is 3,087. docs/CRATES.md records both tool decisions. orb-9o6 makes no docs/CONTRACTS.md or CHANGELOG.md change; concurrent architecture-document edits are independently user-authorized and do not become governance proof. Exact verification passed locally: cargo fmt --all --check; cargo check --locked --workspace; cargo test --locked --workspace with 19 tests; cargo run --locked --quiet -p orbit-governance -- .; isolated cargo install --git https://github.com/luccahuguet/starcompass.git --rev 9d119c235cd3d9f5a2b996e54f37a96a9640f679 --locked followed by check-consumer; cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; actionlint .github/workflows/ci.yml; LOC assertions; git diff --check. title: Audit Orbit cross-subsystem integration
description:
## Contract routing

This is a read-only repository audit. It changes no ORB product contract, implements no feature or fix, and authorizes no dependency, compatibility surface, or public behavior. Audit one exact accepted revision and preserve all pre-existing worktree state.

## Why

Feature-local fresh-eyes and simplification passes can converge even when the owner loop, protocol, presentation, and platform seam each pass but end-to-end contracts, governance, or consumers drift. Repository integration is a distinct failure domain, so it needs one bounded cross-subsystem review.

## Evidence

- `README.md:8`: the accepted Orbit slice combines every subsystem into one product claim
- `docs/RATIONALE.md:49`: the one-authority hypothesis defines the cross-subsystem flow
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:18`: ORB-C1 through ORB-C10 route accepted behavior and proofs
- `tools/governance/src/main.rs:1`: repository governance checks durable planning and proof metadata

## Prerequisites and reference gate

- All four declared local subsystem audits must be complete. Record the exact Venus and Eon consumer revisions reviewed; consumer audit completion is not a prerequisite because Orbit owns the upstream contract, but any discovered boundary change must follow the explicit compatibility and update-order gate.
- Route unresolved terminal, lifecycle, protocol, dependency, portability, or ownership questions through `docs/REFERENCES.md`, the applicable contract proofs, `docs/RATIONALE.md`, `docs/CRATES.md`, and exact consumer sources. Record exact identities, accepted mechanisms, rejected surrounding scope, ownership consequences, and the cheapest check. Reuse prior evidence only when the question and exact revision still match.

## Scope

In scope:
- All four Orbit subsystem audit records and the complete accepted runtime path.
- README, contracts, rationale, references, crate decisions, stack boundaries, changelog, governance tool, formatter counterexamples, lifecycle tests, and exact Venus/Eon consumers.
- Cross-owner lifecycle and failure semantics, duplicate policy, proof freshness, portability, dependency weight, test gaps/redundancy, and documentation/Beads reconciliation.
- End-to-end checks at one exact accepted revision without widening claims to macOS, restart persistence, multiple clients, or deferred protocol planes.

Out of scope:
- Implementing, fixing, refactoring, or editing repository files.
- Adding or changing product contracts, dependencies, compatibility promises, or deferred features.
- Auditing behavior owned by another repository beyond verifying the consumed boundary.
- Creating remediation Beads unless the user separately authorizes a planning-only batch.

## Audit method

1. Record governing instructions, tracker state, accepted contract proofs, and immutable subject identity: clean HEAD, or HEAD plus a SHA-256 of the tracked binary diff and hashes of every in-scope untracked file. Preserve the exact dirty paths.
2. Read every in-scope owner, its direct callers and consumers, meaningful tests, contract rows, reference decisions, and dependency decisions.
3. Trace the observable flow end to end and audit correctness, failures, bounds, security boundaries, performance, tests, ownership, dependencies, portability, DX, and documentation.
4. Run a fresh-eyes correctness pass, then a separate simplification and ownership pass. Reject style preferences, speculative features, accepted tradeoffs, and duplicates of existing Beads.
5. Vet each remaining finding against exact file:line evidence and record impact, effort (S/M/L), implementation risk, confidence, the cheapest falsifying check, and why it merits action.
6. Repeat the complete review after any material planning correction or subject-snapshot change. Converge only when a final full pass over one unchanged recorded snapshot finds no additional actionable finding beyond the recorded set.
7. Record either the vetted findings or an explicit no-finding result in this Bead with the audited revision, commands, failures, and remaining proof limits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The audit covers the complete stated subsystem and adjacent boundaries, not only recent diffs.
- Every finding is concrete, reproducible or directly evidenced, ownership-routed, and checked against existing Beads.
- No tracked project file or preserved untracked user artifact changes during the audit; generated build outputs do not alter the recorded subject snapshot.
- The final record identifies the exact subject snapshot; any in-scope subject change invalidates prior completion and requires a complete new pass.
- The final pass reports convergence under the declared lenses without widening that claim to runtime or platform behavior not exercised.
- Findings remain recommendations until the user chooses separate remediation work.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `cargo check --locked --workspace` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `cargo test --locked --workspace` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `cargo run --locked --quiet -p orbit-governance -- .` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `git diff --check` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- A prior verification result may be cited instead of rerun only when its recorded subject snapshot, environment, command, and exercised surface match exactly; otherwise rerun it.
- `br sync --flush-only` should persist the audit record without changing implementation.
- Final status and diff inspection should show only the pre-existing worktree plus authorized Beads mutations.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if an active implementation owns or materially changes an in-scope surface.
- Stop if evidence requires a new contract, dependency decision, cross-repository owner change, or scope expansion.
- Stop and report rather than compensating for an upstream or downstream contract gap.

title: Audit the Orbit authoritative owner loop

## Contract routing

This is a read-only repository audit. It changes no ORB product contract, implements no feature or fix, and authorizes no dependency, compatibility surface, or public behavior. Audit one exact accepted revision and preserve all pre-existing worktree state.

## Why

Feature-local fresh-eyes and simplification passes can converge while PTY, terminal, client, input, selection, revision, queue, and exit states can form unsafe combinations. This subsystem owns a distinct invariant and failure domain, so it needs one bounded whole-subsystem review that includes direct callers and consumers.

## Evidence

- `src/main.rs:133`: one synchronous loop composes terminal, PTY, listener, client, selection, and revision state
- `src/main.rs:348`: incremental client input and fatal protocol handling enter the same owner
- `src/main.rs:406`: semantic actions mutate authoritative state and bounded queues
- `tests/lifecycle.rs:396`: real subprocess checks begin at negotiation and lifecycle races

## Prerequisites and reference gate

- There is no planning dependency beyond a stable in-scope subject. Do not start while another issue or agent is changing an in-scope surface.
- Route each terminal, lifecycle, protocol, dependency, portability, or ownership question through `docs/REFERENCES.md`; read the applicable contract proofs, `docs/RATIONALE.md`, `docs/CRATES.md`, and exact primary or comparison sources for the question. Record exact identities, accepted mechanisms, rejected surrounding scope, ownership consequences, and the cheapest check in this Bead. Reuse prior evidence only when the question and exact revision still match.

## Scope

In scope:
- `src/main.rs` outside presentation extraction and platform implementation details.
- Every owner-loop unit test and `tests/lifecycle.rs` contract path.
- ORB-C1 through ORB-C5 and ORB-C7 through ORB-C9 as routed to the owner loop.
- Negotiation, attachment exclusivity, terminal/PTY closure, selection, input encoding, revision changes, backpressure, fairness, and shutdown.

Out of scope:
- Implementing, fixing, refactoring, or editing repository files.
- Adding or changing product contracts, dependencies, compatibility promises, or deferred features.
- Auditing behavior owned by another repository beyond verifying the consumed boundary.
- Creating remediation Beads unless the user separately authorizes a planning-only batch.

## Audit method

1. Record governing instructions, tracker state, accepted contract proofs, and immutable subject identity: clean HEAD, or HEAD plus a SHA-256 of the tracked binary diff and hashes of every in-scope untracked file. Preserve the exact dirty paths.
2. Read every in-scope owner, its direct callers and consumers, meaningful tests, contract rows, reference decisions, and dependency decisions.
3. Trace the observable flow end to end and audit correctness, failures, bounds, security boundaries, performance, tests, ownership, dependencies, portability, DX, and documentation.
4. Run a fresh-eyes correctness pass, then a separate simplification and ownership pass. Reject style preferences, speculative features, accepted tradeoffs, and duplicates of existing Beads.
5. Vet each remaining finding against exact file:line evidence and record impact, effort (S/M/L), implementation risk, confidence, the cheapest falsifying check, and why it merits action.
6. Repeat the complete review after any material planning correction or subject-snapshot change. Converge only when a final full pass over one unchanged recorded snapshot finds no additional actionable finding beyond the recorded set.
7. Record either the vetted findings or an explicit no-finding result in this Bead with the audited revision, commands, failures, and remaining proof limits.

## Acceptance

- The audit covers the complete stated subsystem and adjacent boundaries, not only recent diffs.
- Every finding is concrete, reproducible or directly evidenced, ownership-routed, and checked against existing Beads.
- No tracked project file or preserved untracked user artifact changes during the audit; generated build outputs do not alter the recorded subject snapshot.
- The final record identifies the exact subject snapshot; any in-scope subject change invalidates prior completion and requires a complete new pass.
- The final pass reports convergence under the declared lenses without widening that claim to runtime or platform behavior not exercised.
- Findings remain recommendations until the user chooses separate remediation work.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `cargo check --locked --workspace` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `cargo test --locked --workspace` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `cargo run --locked --quiet -p orbit-governance -- .` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `git diff --check` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- A prior verification result may be cited instead of rerun only when its recorded subject snapshot, environment, command, and exercised surface match exactly; otherwise rerun it.
- `br sync --flush-only` should persist the audit record without changing implementation.
- Final status and diff inspection should show only the pre-existing worktree plus authorized Beads mutations.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if an active implementation owns or materially changes an in-scope surface.
- Stop if evidence requires a new contract, dependency decision, cross-repository owner change, or scope expansion.
- Stop and report rather than compensating for an upstream or downstream contract gap.

Audit completed on 2026-08-13 against immutable Orbit edge revision 7d34399b15496513f7f91b94acd32e8d04389e16. The complete protocol package and exact Venus consumer review converged with three actionable recommendations. No implementation, contract, dependency, compatibility, proof, or project-document change is authorized by this result.

Finding 1 — ORBF v1 capability semantics are not enforced by their canonical owner.
Evidence: crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:130-135 defines public hyperlink and Kitty graphics booleans; encode_frame writes either value at 375-388; decode_frame accepts either canonical boolean at 425-451; validate_frame at 549-578 never validates capabilities. The exact Orbit producer is fixed to hyperlinks=true and kitty_graphics=false at src/presentation.rs:134-146, and README.md:97-101 plus ORB-C6 declare that v1 advertises hyperlinks and does not support Kitty graphics. The dependency-free package therefore encodes and decodes capability claims that the accepted v1 producer cannot truthfully provide, including kitty_graphics=true; it also has no central rule for a disabled hyperlink capability combined with non-empty cell hyperlinks.
Impact: Medium. A canonical consumer can accept a contradictory or unsupported rich-presentation claim, weakening the ORB-C6 boundary instead of failing at the shared codec.
Effort: S. Implementation risk: Medium because tightening accepted bytes is a protocol-compatibility question and must be owner-first.
Confidence: 0.96.
Cheapest falsifying check: construct an ORBF v1 Frame with kitty_graphics=true, and separately hyperlinks=false with a non-empty cell hyperlink; encode and decode currently succeed. A focused contract test should first settle and assert the one accepted semantic combination or relationship.
Why action merits consideration: this is trust-boundary validation of a proved contract, not style. No existing open or deferred Bead owns current ORBF v1 capability validation; the deferred graphics epic owns a future revision, not this invariant.

Finding 2 — the advertised ORBS version-range negotiation is unreachable for a real header-version mismatch.
Evidence: ClientMessage::Hello and ServerMessage::Incompatible describe revision-range negotiation at crates/protocol/src/session.rs:141-174, but message_len rejects any header version other than VERSION before decoding the Hello payload at 572-597. The owner loop consequently converts an actual old or future header into generic Failure(Protocol) at src/main.rs:653-672; only a current-v3 header can reach the overlap test and typed Incompatible response at 705-726. The lifecycle incompatibility case at tests/lifecycle.rs:455-470 uses a v3 encoder with a non-overlapping payload range, so it does not exercise a v2 or future header. Since server responses also use the exact current header, an older client cannot decode the nominal typed incompatibility response.
Impact: Medium. Stale exact consumers receive a generic undecodable protocol failure, while the typed range surface and version-negotiated wording promise behavior the wire envelope cannot deliver.
Effort: M. Implementation risk: High because the smallest honest resolution requires an explicit choice between exact-version framing with simpler messages and a stable negotiation envelope; no compatibility window is implied.
Confidence: 0.99.
Cheapest falsifying check: encode Hello, change only header bytes 4..6 to VERSION-1 while leaving a payload range that includes VERSION, and assert current client_message_len returns UnsupportedVersion before Hello can be decoded.
Why action merits consideration: this is dead compatibility flexibility plus misleading failure semantics in the shared owner. Exact pinning limits normal exposure but does not make the protocol surface coherent. No existing Bead matches this issue.

Finding 3 — Orbit current-state documentation has not reconciled the exact Venus ORBS v3 adoption.
Evidence: README.md:21-25 and 219-225 plus docs/CRATES.md:17 still say Venus consumes ORBS v2 and has not adopted v3. docs/CONTRACTS.md:115-119 still phrases adoption as future, while ORB-C9 at line 37 names a healthy ORBS v2 attachment even though current Orbit accepts only v3 and v3 preserves the selection messages. The exact Venus repository at current edge 6966ec0fd6761f17892004fb3a36a3d030ef5177 pins Orbit 3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174 in Cargo.toml:13 and records partial VEN-C13 v3 consumption in docs/CONTRACTS.md:16,23-26. Historical v2 proof rows remain valid lineage and should not be rewritten as current v3 proofs.
Impact: Low to Medium. Agents and integration reviewers are directed to a completed consumer-adoption gap and can misroute follow-up work or misstate the current wire boundary.
Effort: S. Implementation risk: Low; this is factual current-state reconciliation, preserving historical proof identities and the still-open native dogfood or Eon acceptance gaps.
Confidence: 0.99.
Cheapest falsifying check: compare the exact Venus manifest pin and VEN-C13 row with the named Orbit README, contract, and crate-decision statements.
Why action merits consideration: canonical docs are the planning and compatibility source of truth. No matching open or deferred Bead exists.

No additional finding survived the audit for frame or message size accounting, pre-allocation bounds, truncation and trailing-byte handling, role tags, typed key/modifier/mouse/resize/selection domains, strict FrameReducer ordering, libghostty key mapping, dependency footprint, unsafe code, or platform coupling.

title: Prove Orbit as the durable terminal runtime beneath Venus
description: Determine whether a small Rust and libghostty runtime can provide Yazelix Eon with the PTY and session-lifetime role that Zellij provides in Yazelix Nova's current Mars and Zellij chain, beneath Eon's greenfield Venus graphical client. Yazelix Nova remains an independent product and the comparison baseline. The authorized experiment is Linux-only, local, one-session, and one-active-client. Either a go or no-go result completes the architectural experiment.
design:
docs/RATIONALE.md records the origin, ownership hypothesis, tradeoffs, and stop criteria. docs/REFERENCES.md maps prior art to the slice where it can answer a concrete question. Each implementation bead performs that source review just in time and records the release or commit studied, the contract or failure mode extracted, and the surrounding scope rejected. Yazelix Eon is the permanent name of the separate greenfield Yazelix line, and Venus is the permanent name of its graphical client. Yazelix Nova remains an independently valuable product on Mars and Zellij; Mars and Mars Next remain behavioral references only. The orb-bi4.1 decision makes Orbit the sole owner of PTY and libghostty terminal state. Clients receive host-authored structured presentation frames and send semantic input; they do not reconstruct terminal state from Formatter output or raw PTY tails. The boundary must preserve a path to rich terminal presentation and, after separate graduation and scope decisions, host-owned durable workspace topology for native, web, or mobile clients. The authorized experiment itself remains Linux-only, local, one-session, and one-active-client. `orb-bi4.3` passed the repository boundary gate. The private `Yazelix/eon-desktop` repository owns graphical implementation through Venus; Venus `ven-upt.1` owns the backend/composition decision and `ven-upt.2` owns graphical implementation. Orbit `orb-bi4.4` is the cross-repository acceptance tracker, and graphical Venus code does not enter Orbit. The proven structured presentation contract is the cross-repository boundary. The naming and long-term architecture decisions do not authorize multiplayer, remote transport, layouts, tabs, plugins, a configuration framework, daemon-restart persistence, or unapproved libghostty forks or wrappers in the initial experiment.

The accepted foundation proves ORB-C1 through ORB-C9 at 9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757 and ORB-C10 at 292b2451c9a1d99390334771a681c7f481c996f2. Orbit distribution revision 00b136318bea13e3f08d490468f069de6f6b9bd2 preserves them; Venus 2d36c72dc87ca5416e22d6afdc35c6ab4e2fb832 consumes canonical ORBF v1 and ORBS v2; Eon composition proof eae70e8d3ed4348b389f320dfd49d7db29478546 pins the accepted pair. orb-bi4.8 records the user GO and orb-bi4.7 selects eon-pxn as the sole post-graduation frontier. Every dependency in this experiment tree is closed. Final documentation reconciliation aligns the Orbit README, crate index, and changelog with Venus ORBS v2 consumption and aligns the VEN-C3 and VEN-C4 gap columns with proved ORB-C7 while preserving their original consumed proof revisions. It changes no runtime, contract, dependency, proof revision, or Bead graph.

2. orb-bi4.8 records an explicit user go or no-go decision for the Venus and Orbit direction.
3. On a go decision, orb-bi4.7 records the sequencing and ownership of post-graduation workspace and client expansions before implementation planning. On a no-go decision, orb-bi4.7 closes as not applicable.

Exceptions remain audit-visible and are not represented as successful gates.
7. The final plan treats Yazelix Eon as a separate greenfield line, Venus as distinct from Mars, and Yazelix Nova as an independently valuable Mars and Zellij product that this experiment does not modify or replace.
8. The experiment proves one authoritative terminal with rich structured presentation rather than a text-grid-only, Formatter-checkpoint, or raw-tail replication ceiling.
9. After orb-bi4.3 passes, Venus ven-upt.2 owns graphical implementation in the Yazelix/eon-desktop repository; Orbit orb-bi4.4 accepts that exact consumer proof, and no graphical Venus code enters Orbit.

Every product implementation Bead follows the required Execution baseline, Reference gate, and triggered Crate gate ordering, or records an explicit user-approved Protocol exception for the missed rule. An exception is not represented as compliance, inherited by another Bead, or used to broaden scope.
