title: Prove the libghostty attachment model
description: Answer the highest-risk question before building runtime architecture: can the released libghostty-vt Rust API support one headless authoritative terminal and reconstruct a second terminal that continues correctly from an ordered PTY tail?
design: Use the current released libghostty-vt crate and record the exact version and source. Start by reproducing the zmx-style VT bootstrap through the public Formatter and FormatterOptions APIs because the current Rust binding exposes terminal modes and other reconstruction options. Compare direct state export and import only if the current source exposes it; use bounded checkpoint plus raw replay only as a fallback, and reject unbounded history replay. Account for the unstable API, single-thread ownership of !Send and !Sync terminal objects, terminal-generated PTY responses, and the boundary between semantic input events and encoded bytes. Only Orbit may answer terminal queries back to the PTY. Test hidden state that can alter future bytes, including cursor and keyboard modes, pending wrap, alternate and inactive screens, tab stops, character sets, palette and hyperlinks, scrollback required for future resize, and a parser between escape-sequence bytes. Stop for a user decision before adding a fork, compatibility layer, substantial wrapper, or alternative engine.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A minimal Linux Rust proof builds against a recorded released libghostty-vt version with the real feature enabled by default.
2. The proof feeds deterministic VT input into authoritative state and reconstructs a second terminal through the public VT formatter, or records a reproducible reason that strategy fails before trying a fallback.
3. A distinguishing future tail produces equivalent semantic behavior, including hidden modes rather than only equal visible cells.
4. The proof covers attachment while the alternate screen is active followed by exit to the primary screen, and attachment at split points inside escape, UTF-8, and APC or graphics sequences.
5. The result states which active and inactive screen, scrollback, mode, parser, effect, input-encoding, palette, hyperlink, and image state the strategy preserves or loses.
6. The result records thread ownership, required callbacks, dependency footprint, Rust LOC, and the exact reference releases or commits studied.
7. Failure identifies the missing API and a reproducible counterexample; it does not introduce a fork, second terminal engine, or unbounded replay.
notes: Proof result on 2026-08-04: the public formatter path FAILS the exact Orbit attachment contract. The implementation pins crates.io libghostty-vt 0.2.1 with default features and libghostty-vt-sys 0.2.1. Artifact SHA-256 values are 6219ed1c364b3ef5815fb0fd2acc0662f792adc706dabf59b7ca89280ee6d066 and 865fed12a8b2bba3507b3bccd0bef439e06ef1100e652fe6b71d132c41ee8db0. The sys crate pins Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083. The published dependency builds locally with Rust 1.96.0 and Zig 0.15.2. Current libghostty-rs head 72ac98f292879bf9f788fcbb11238c562a1eebe6 has moved to a later Ghostty source requiring Zig 0.16 and was reference evidence only. Tests use one thread as the owner of both !Send and !Sync terminals. The authoritative terminal alone installs on_pty_write; the reconstructed terminal intentionally has no PTY callback, and a DSR query produces exactly one captured response. No other callback is required by the deterministic corpus. Reproducible public-API counterexamples: attaching while alternate is active reconstructs its visible content but loses the inactive primary, so a shared 1049l tail reveals primary text only on the authority; CUP cursor replay loses pending wrap, so the next printable byte diverges; prefixes split inside CSI, four-byte UTF-8, and APC all diverge under a shared suffix because formatter output carries no persistent parser or decoder continuation; full tab-stop replay moves the reconstructed cursor from column 1 to column 4; exact scrollback accounting differs at 5 versus 4 rows even though the checked visible history plus resize tail converges; closed-cell hyperlink URI metadata, OSC title, and Kitty image storage are absent after bootstrap. Checked successes: active text, DECCKM, Kitty keyboard flags, palette, working directory, state-aware Up-key encoding, custom tab behavior after explicit repositioning, charset state, and a currently active hyperlink for future text when tab-stop replay is omitted. Unclassified in this proof: current SGR style, scrolling-region state, and character-protection state; do not infer preservation or loss for them. The public safe binding exposes no inactive-screen formatter, terminal clone, checkpoint, export/import, or serialize/deserialize API. Cargo locks ten third-party crates including the binding, sys crate, and proc-macro stack. By default, the sys crate runs git clone for its pinned Ghostty source when GHOSTTY_SOURCE_DIR is unset and may let Zig resolve packages from the network unless GHOSTTY_ZIG_SYSTEM_DIR supplies a prefetched package set. The local proof build produced an approximately 155 MiB Ghostty source checkout outside owned Rust LOC. Future Nix packaging must prefetch both the Ghostty source and Zig package inputs. Owned Rust is 282 lines: the one-line binary plus 281 test lines. Verification passes cargo fmt --check, cargo check, cargo test with eight contract tests, and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings. References audited: zmx 4f3739ef98f44d0b639afa57fd76bffcad5d0ef4, Ghostling f9034e43a50a2f3a8101e35497f486090c1ddd6e, libghostty-rs 72ac98f292879bf9f788fcbb11238c562a1eebe6, released Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083, and vt100 0.16.2. No fork, binding extension, compatibility wrapper, second terminal engine, bounded or unbounded replay fallback, PTY, socket, or protocol code was added. The decision is not binary: user choices include pursuing an upstream checkpoint/export-import API; changing to structured server-rendered frames; approving a binding extension, fork, or substantial wrapper; comparing another terminal engine; relaxing the exact attachment contract; or stopping the experiment. Bounded raw replay without an exact checkpoint cannot support arbitrarily long sessions while remaining bounded, so it is not a standalone solution to the current contract. The proof stopped at the required decision boundary. User decision after the proof: adopt host-authored structured presentation frames and stop pursuing a reconstructed client terminal plus raw-PTY-tail replication. Orbit retains the sole authoritative libghostty terminal and sole PTY-response callback. A client receives a coherent complete presentation frame followed by ordered frame revisions and sends semantic input for Orbit to encode against authoritative state. The presentation boundary must not become a text-grid ceiling: it must explicitly account for styled cells and graphemes, cursor, title and working directory, hyperlinks, and graphics resources or capabilities. orb-bi4.3 must prove the smallest public read-only extraction surface and stop for another user decision before any binding extension, fork, substantial wrapper, or alternative engine. Full terminal checkpoint export/import, Formatter-as-checkpoint, a second client terminal emulator, and bounded or unbounded raw replay are rejected for the current direction. The initial experiment remains Linux-only, local, one session, and one active client. The long-term contract must not preclude host-owned durable workspace topology or native, web, and mobile clients, but multiple sessions, windows, tabs, splits, remote transport, web, and mobile implementation remain outside the current experiment.
close_reason: Completed: eight contract tests conclusively disprove Formatter checkpoint plus raw-tail replication; dependency and state-loss evidence is recorded, and the user selected sole Orbit terminal authority with host-authored structured presentation frames as the next architecture.

title: Own the typed local-session codec in orbit-protocol
description: Add the canonical local-session protocol boundary required by Venus: versioned and bounded attach outcomes, frame envelopes, semantic key, mouse, focus, arbitrary paste, resize, and compatibility messages owned by orbit-protocol and consumed by Orbit itself.
design:
Extend the existing std-only orbit-protocol 0.1.0 package with one local-session module and one framed version-1 message codec. The package owns stable platform-neutral message values and bounds; Orbit alone maps accepted input into libghostty terminal encoding and PTY resize. Replace the private line protocol in the server, diagnostic client, and lifecycle checks in one coordinated Orbit revision because that syntax has no accepted external consumer. The stream uses one magic, version, kind, and bounded-length envelope; typed messages cover handshake and compatibility, attach outcomes, complete ORBF frames, acknowledgements and bounded failures, semantic input, and resize. ORBF bytes remain owned by the existing frame codec and are not reinterpreted by the session layer.

Use TDD in orbit-protocol and keep the implementation dependency-free. Do not add a generated schema, package, binary, async runtime, remote transport, multiple clients, compatibility window, or graphical surface. The user-approved boundary changes and hardens ORB-C3, ORB-C4, and ORB-C5 while preserving ORB-C1, ORB-C2, ORB-C6, and the current ORB-C7 limits. The replacement is breaking only for private diagnostic syntax; update every known in-repository consumer atomically, and require Venus to pin the accepted proof revision.
acceptance_criteria:
1. An Execution baseline records HEAD, AGENTS.md hash, updated_at, ORB-C3 through ORB-C5 as changed or hardened, ORB-C1, ORB-C2, ORB-C6, and ORB-C7 as preserved, intended surfaces, dirty paths, and agent identity.
2. A pre-code Reference gate records exact Orbit, libghostty-vt, zmx, FrankenTerm, Qwertty, and comparison-only Foot identities, accepted mechanisms, rejected scope, ownership consequences, and the first check. No Crate gate is triggered because the accepted package and standard library remain sufficient.
3. orbit-protocol owns one documented version-1 local-session envelope with fixed magic, version, typed message kind, bounded payload length, strict decoding, and no external dependency.
4. Typed server messages represent attachment accepted, busy, incompatible revision, complete canonical ORBF frame, request accepted, bounded request failure, and session exit. Typed client messages represent hello, complete semantic key events, mouse, focus, arbitrary paste bytes, and resize.
5. Key events preserve action, physical key identity, modifiers, consumed modifiers, composition state, optional UTF-8 text, and unshifted codepoint. Mouse events preserve action, optional button, modifiers, and finite nonnegative surface coordinates.
6. Decoding rejects invalid magic, unsupported versions, unknown kinds, invalid flags or tags, malformed UTF-8, invalid codepoints or modifier bits, impossible dimensions, non-finite or negative coordinates, oversize declarations, truncation, and trailing payload bytes before payload-sized allocation.
7. Orbit server, diagnostic client, output queue, and lifecycle checks use only the canonical codec for the local-session boundary; the old line parser and frame-header construction are removed rather than retained as a compatibility path.
8. Focused unit checks round-trip every message family and cover corrupt, truncated, oversized, embedded-newline paste, ordinary text input, modified keys, all mouse buttons, compatibility rejection, and complete-frame transport.
9. Real-PTY lifecycle checks prove attachment, deterministic busy rejection, ordinary text and special-key input, arbitrary multiline paste, mouse, focus, resize, reconnect, exit, and socket cleanup without weakening existing ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 evidence.
10. Closure records platform-neutral disposition, owned LOC and dependency footprint, exact verification, compatibility classification and update order, contract proof status, remaining limits, README scorecard, and changelog disposition.
notes:
Accepted at 838b67652c4df1979e599b9c401ee664ffac66bd after the fourteenth bounded fresh-eyes and simplification repair was folded into the single orb-bi4.10 implementation. The dependency-free orbit-protocol package solely owns ORBS v1 and ORBF v1; Orbit solely maps accepted semantic input and resize values into authoritative libghostty state and the PTY.

Canonical mouse axes and surface pixel dimensions remain bounded to the selected terminal mapper u16 domain. Exact u16::MAX values remain accepted; larger values fail through InvalidCoordinates or InvalidSurfaceSize before checked native coordinate conversion. The wire layout and field types remain unchanged.

All fatal framing, decode, compatibility, and message-order transitions now use one Client-owned close-when-flushed operation. It drops unread client input and its backing allocation immediately, then preserves the existing bounded failure-response drain and close timing. A malformed correctly framed mouse regression proves the exact Failure(Protocol, invalid mouse coordinates), terminal close fact, zero input length, and zero retained capacity. Normal successful input buffering and output ordering are unchanged.

Known-closed PTY admission remains fail closed. At the existing open-to-closed transition, Orbit drops the sole queued-write VecDeque, releasing both undeliverable bytes and retained allocation. Later semantic requests return Failure(Terminal, PTY is closed) and do not rebuild the queue. Orbit still waits for and reaps the exact known child.

ORB-C1 through ORB-C6 are proved at 838b67652c4df1979e599b9c401ee664ffac66bd. ORB-C7 remains Partially proved with strict pre-allocation and mapper-domain bounds, bounded queues and frame history, terminal-closing exclusions, fatal-client input-storage release, and closed-PTY queued-byte plus retained-storage release; orb-bi4.5 retains sustained-pressure and adversarial-cleanup work.

Compatibility is a compatible resource-lifetime hardening. Valid ORBS v1 and ORBF v1 bytes and values, fatal Failure bytes and details, output order, close-after-flush timing, PTY and terminal effects, presentation, logs, dependency graph, and platform observations are unchanged. No accepted external consumer migration is required; Venus must pin 838b67652c4df1979e599b9c401ee664ffac66bd.

No package, manifest, lockfile, dependency, generated artifact, native build, CI, Nix, graphical surface, wire revision, or platform surface changed. orbit-protocol remains std-only at 2,939 Rust lines: 2,026 production and 913 tests. Product Rust and tests total 5,645 lines, governance remains 765, and total owned Rust is 6,410. The repair is neutral above the existing isolated Linux PTY seam and adds no macOS blocker.

Exact clean detached Linux proof at 838b67652c4df1979e599b9c401ee664ffac66bd with Rust 1.96.0 passed cargo fmt --all --check; cargo check --locked --workspace; cargo test --locked --workspace with 4 governance, 15 protocol, 12 owner-loop/platform/presentation, 8 Formatter, and 5 real-PTY lifecycle checks; cargo run --locked --quiet -p orbit-governance -- .; cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo tree --locked -p orbit-protocol; source-independent Starcompass validation; exact f41e799db9d78277f18409985287e96a6fc80f51 source-backed Starcompass validation; clean-worktree validation; and commit diff checking.

The simplification leaves one terminal transition owner rather than five duplicated writes and rejects a larger lifecycle enum, element-only clear, shrink-to-fit policy, ordinary input shrinking, OutputQueue redesign, timeout, allocator page-return or zeroization claim, sustained-backpressure work, new dependency, legacy compatibility, remote or multiple clients, and source copying. Remaining product limits are one local client, complete-frame v1, partial ORB-C7 sustained-pressure proof, unsupported Kitty graphics, and no remote transport, restart persistence, packaging, or graphical surface.

title: Prove PTY lifetime across diagnostic-client disconnect
description: Build the smallest headless Orbit vertical slice that proves process persistence and local transport. Orbit owns one real PTY shell and one authoritative libghostty terminal on a single owner thread. One diagnostic client connects over a local Unix socket. Structured presentation attachment and convergence remain the outcome of orb-bi4.3.
design: Keep one Rust package and binary unless evidence establishes another owner. Use the sole-authority and thread model accepted in orb-bi4.1; do not reconstruct terminal state in the client or establish raw PTY bytes as the client contract. Before proposing a PTY dependency, compare portable-pty with the smallest direct rustix or Linux implementation for lifecycle control, dependency footprint, owned LOC, and testability; study zmx, shpool, abduco, and tastty for concrete process and socket failure behavior. Keep the server in the foreground for the experiment; daemonization policy is deferred. Use a minimal bounded diagnostic message set rather than a general protocol framework. The client sends semantic key, mouse, focus, paste, and resize events; Orbit encodes them against authoritative terminal state and alone owns terminal-generated PTY writes. The active client controls PTY size, and the server retains the last size while detached. Place the socket in a user-private runtime location and define stale-socket cleanup.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A subprocess check starts a real shell, attaches a diagnostic client, exchanges semantic input and diagnostic output, and changes PTY size.
2. Client disconnect leaves the shell and foreground process alive; output produced while detached reaches authoritative server state.
3. A later diagnostic connection reaches the same live PTY. This is a lifecycle smoke test, not presentation-convergence proof.
4. A second simultaneous attach receives one deterministic rejection without disturbing the active client.
5. Child exit, server shutdown, signal handling, process reaping, socket permissions, and stale-socket cleanup have explicit checked behavior.
6. Checks use observable synchronization and bounded timeouts rather than sleep as a correctness mechanism.
7. The result records the zmx, shpool, abduco, tastty, portable-pty, and rustix releases or commits inspected, the lifecycle lessons used, and why the selected PTY level is smaller for this contract.
8. Focused checks verify that Orbit, not the client, performs state-aware key and mouse encoding and owns focus and paste encoding; this does not create a general input protocol.
9. A pre-implementation, append-only `Reference gate` comment satisfies AGENTS.md before the first implementation edit, and closure evidence satisfies the AGENTS.md closure gate.

Current candidate evidence (2026-08-04):
- Protocol state: comments 22 and 23 record this run's execution baseline and reference gate before its test edit. The user then clarified AGENTS.md so future read-only review happens before run comments and the gates begin only after a concrete edit candidate exists. The existing append-only comments remain factual. This run did not invoke or extend the one-time retroactive exception for the original candidate.
- Ownership and scope: one foreground Linux process, package, binary, and owner thread own one real PTY child, one nonblocking master, one libghostty-vt terminal, one private Unix listener, and at most one bounded diagnostic client. No raw PTY attachment, presentation frame, daemon, library split, general protocol, module, dependency, feature, contract, or planning bead was added.
- Contract routing: ORB-C1 and ORB-C2 were inspected for regressions; ORB-C3 and ORB-C5 remain observably preserved. ORB-C4, ORB-C6, and ORB-C7 remain outside this bead. All affected contracts remain Partially proved until the user accepts and authorizes an immutable proof-bearing commit.
- Exact references inspected across the candidate and fresh-eyes runs: libghostty-vt/sys 0.2.1 and pinned Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083; zmx 4f3739ef98f44d0b639afa57fd76bffcad5d0ef4; shpool 901e18c3ced010073178b78c0ca2a8cdd43e8581; abduco 8c32909a159aaa9484c82b71f05b7a73321eb491; tastty 0.1.1; portable-pty 0.9.0; rustix 1.1.4; rustix-openpty 0.2.0; comparison-only nix 0.31.3; and Rust 1.96 standard-library Child, Command, and SIGPIPE behavior.
- Crate decision: retain direct libc 0.2.189 for the candidate. Nix still needs explicit CLOEXEC and ioctl work and has no demonstrated net owned-LOC reduction; rustix-openpty adds layers and packages; portable-pty imposes a broader ownership model. The normal dependency graph is unchanged, and the fresh-eyes runs did not edit Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock.
- Confirmed production regressions fixed in prior passes: final child PTY output reaches authoritative libghostty state before exit publication; startup signal cleanup owns the socket; aborted ATTACHED writes cannot terminate Orbit; shutdown reaps a distinct foreground process group; and SocketGuard does not remove a later socket identity.

title: Prove atomic structured presentation convergence on reattach
description: Implement the defining Orbit attachment contract on the real PTY slice: Orbit remains the sole authoritative libghostty terminal, and an attaching client receives one coherent complete host-authored presentation frame followed by ordered frame revisions. The client never reconstructs terminal authority from Formatter output or raw PTY bytes.
design: Use the authority and lifecycle model proven in orb-bi4.1 and orb-bi4.2. First determine the smallest public read-only libghostty surface that can produce a structured presentation frame; study Ghostling, libghostty-rs, and justerm-core at recorded revisions. Formatter output may be evidence but is not a checkpoint or client protocol. Serialize PTY reads, authoritative terminal mutation, frame extraction, and publication through one owner so attachment has no race window. Start with complete coalesced frames carrying a monotonic revision rather than premature deltas. The representation must not silently flatten the terminal to plain text: account explicitly for dimensions, styled cells and graphemes, cursor, active screen, title and working directory, hyperlinks, and graphics resources or declared capabilities. Hidden terminal state such as inactive screens, pending wrap, parser continuation, scrollback semantics, and terminal-generated responses stays exclusively in Orbit; later frames must reflect its visible consequences. The client sends semantic input and never runs a second terminal emulator or answers the PTY. Keep the initial protocol local, one-session, one-client, and bounded. It may leave workspace topology and remote transport for later while avoiding a text-grid-only architectural ceiling. If the public API cannot expose the minimum presentation state, record the exact missing read-only API and stop for user choice before a binding extension, fork, substantial wrapper, or alternative engine.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A real PTY establishes authoritative terminal state, emits output while detached, and continues output while a client attaches.
2. The first attach message is one coherent complete presentation frame at revision N; output racing attachment is reflected either in that frame or a later strictly ordered revision, with no duplicate revision or stale final state.
3. The checked presentation corpus covers styled text, Unicode and graphemes, cursor state, active and alternate screens, title, working directory, hyperlinks, and graphics capability or resource handling; unsupported state is explicit rather than silently discarded.
4. Counterexamples from orb-bi4.1—an inactive primary screen, pending wrap, and parser splits inside CSI, UTF-8, and APC or graphics input—remain correct because their hidden state stays in Orbit and their later visible effects appear in subsequent frames.
5. Varying PTY read chunk boundaries and attaching during output does not change the eventual authoritative presentation.
6. Complete frames are bounded and coalesced; a slow diagnostic client cannot cause unbounded history or block authoritative PTY processing indefinitely.
7. The proof uses no client-side terminal reconstruction, raw-tail replication contract, Formatter checkpoint, second terminal engine, fork, or unbounded replay.
8. The result records exact libghostty, Ghostling, libghostty-rs, and justerm-core releases or commits, the public extraction APIs used, owned Rust LOC, dependency cost, and any missing minimum read-only surface that requires a new user decision.
9. A pre-implementation, append-only `Reference gate` comment satisfies AGENTS.md before the first implementation edit, and closure evidence satisfies the AGENTS.md closure gate.
10. Before implementation, an Execution baseline freezes the Bead revision, governing instructions, contract routing, intended surfaces, and pre-existing dirty paths.
11. Any proposed direct dependency, dependency-feature expansion, engine replacement, or crate-backed oracle passes the Crate gate; using only existing libghostty dependencies is recorded as the no-new-crate decision.
12. Closure classifies ORB-C2, ORB-C4, ORB-C5, ORB-C6, and ORB-C7 as proved, hardened, preserved, or still partial; accepted proof names the exact proof-bearing commit and canonical checks.
13. The resulting structured-presentation boundary is classified for cross-repository compatibility before Venus consumes it.

acceptance_criteria:
1. Aborted, raced, and simultaneous attachment attempts preserve exactly one active client; rejection does not disturb the accepted client or PTY.
2. Client disconnect or crash leaves the live PTY/session available for coherent reattachment while Orbit remains running.
3. PTY EOF, foreground or known-child exit, server shutdown, and supported signals drain or discard owned state according to the indexed contracts without hangs or duplicate terminal actions.
4. Socket and platform resources are cleaned idempotently; stale identity cannot remove another listener or admit an unintended attachment.
5. Slow or failed lifecycle transitions use explicit synchronization and bounded timeouts and leave no abandoned client storage.

notes:
Accepted ownership: the one Orbit owner loop handles known-child exit by invoking the existing Pty cleanup owner before bounded final PTY materialization. Pty holds the live child as Option<Child>; cleanup takes Some to None before signaling and reaping, so later explicit or Drop cleanup is a no-op without an independent stopped flag. Cleanup always signals the owned child process group and any distinct foreground process group even after the leader exits, then kills and reaps the exact known child. Drop remains the fallback on other exits. Steady-state remains one PTY read per readiness turn.

After quiescence, Orbit consumes at most four PTY-master reads and stops earlier on closed/WouldBlock. The zmx measured Linux N_TTY maximum bounds this near 16 KiB. The real-PTY final-state regression emits 5,000 padding bytes before its final OSC title, requiring multiple reads and proving the reproduced final state reaches authoritative libghostty. The continuously writing inherited-PTY descendant regression proves bounded server exit, socket removal, and descendant cleanup. Excess raw output beyond the four-read post-exit budget is deliberately discarded when Pty drops; no client can attach after Exited.

Material rejected exit shapes: one final read lost the title; FIONREAD exposed only the current 4,095-byte chunk and missed later asynchronous PTY transfer; 4 MiB and 64 KiB drain caps let a live producer exceed the lifecycle deadline; stopping process groups followed by an unbounded finite-tail drain still flaked when debug libghostty materialization exceeded five seconds. Quiescence plus the deterministic four-read budget is the smallest shape that preserves the reproduced multi-read final state and the hard shutdown bound. A separate stopped boolean was rejected because Option<Child> directly represents whether cleanup ownership remains.

ORB-C3 negotiation, invalid ordering, simultaneous rejection, abort recovery, and canonical reattachment share one strong lifecycle test. Client holds negotiation_deadline: Option<Instant>; Some means awaiting Hello until the existing one-second deadline and None means attached. This removes the independent attached/timestamp invariant. Other peers receive Busy while negotiation is live; expiry closes the abandoned socket and releases the slot without disturbing the PTY. The canonical validation client retries Unix-socket I/O and pre-attachment Busy responses within its existing five-second deadline. Canonical decode and ordering errors fail immediately: Attached is accepted exactly once, and duplicate Attached or Busy after Attached is rejected. Unbounded reservation, newest-peer eviction, duplicated server attached state, client-side ownership, a timer thread, and an async/state-machine framework were rejected.

The real-PTY detach proof observes PTY resize through the shell title and asserts retained 100x40 dimensions on the reattached client coherent initial frame. Shell PID continuity, deterministic Busy rejection, detached command completion, and owned cleanup remain co-located.

No wire protocol, dependency, manifest, platform abstraction, product boundary, timeout value, or attached-client behavior changes. Product Rust is 5,810 LOC, 64 lines over the prior accepted state. Portability disposition: neutral lifecycle, negotiation-deadline, and quiescence policy with Linux process groups, signals, PTY EOF, poll, and Unix sockets retained in the existing concrete platform seam.

Accepted proof revision 9e9b136969dc583d365daa75402ec03c265080f1 is compatible lifecycle hardening: ORBS v1, ORBF v1, orbit-protocol, manifests, dependencies, and valid client behavior are unchanged, so Venus requires no migration. title: Harden semantic input and resize against authoritative modes
description:
Contract routing:
- Hardens ORB-C5.
- Preserves ORB-C1 through ORB-C4, ORB-C6, and ORB-C7.
- Changes no product feature or compatibility boundary unless the user separately approves it.

Prove the existing canonical key, mouse, focus, arbitrary paste, and resize messages are validated and encoded exactly once against Orbit's authoritative terminal modes and platform seam. This Bead owns Orbit only.
design:
Run after the parser-authority child. Record the Execution baseline and pass the Reference gate before code.

Required before code: exact libghostty-vt input-encoding and mode APIs; zmx Kitty-keyboard failure evidence; and Qwertty keyboard, mouse, paste, resize, and ordered-input mechanisms. Reject raw-byte client input, conventional controlling-terminal ownership, and UI policy.

Exercise ordinary and special keys, modifiers and associated text, mouse modes and held-button semantics, focus, arbitrary multiline paste, attached and detached resize, coordinate/surface bounds, client failure, and mode changes around attachment. Use the existing canonical codec, mapper, and platform seam. Stop for a new input feature, protocol revision, dependency, platform expansion, or Venus correction.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Valid key, mouse, focus, arbitrary paste, and resize messages are encoded exactly once against the authoritative terminal modes.
2. Invalid associated text, modifiers, button states, coordinates, surfaces, paste lengths, and resize values fail deterministically before terminal or platform mutation.
3. Keyboard-protocol and mouse-mode transitions around detach and reattach do not require client-side terminal state.
4. Attached and detached resize preserve coherent grid, PTY pixel sizing, and later input behavior through the existing platform seam.
5. Client failure or terminal closure prevents later queued semantic input from reaching the PTY and releases retained input storage.
6. Orbit is the sole code owner; Venus-native mapping findings are routed separately with exact revisions and compatibility order.
7. Closure advances or explicitly downgrades ORB-C5 at an exact proof revision, regression-checks preserved contracts, and records portability, dependency footprint, LOC, exact verification, and remaining native-client gaps.
notes:
Accepted state

Ownership and code shape: Orbit remains the sole terminal-state and semantic-input encoder. Canonical orbit-protocol validation, libghostty state-derived key, mouse, focus, and paste mapping, FIFO PTY queueing, and the platform resize seam require no production change. One real-PTY lifecycle proof and unique focused validation, pressure, closure, held-button, mapper-domain, and storage-release tests are sufficient.

Ghostty must derive the 100x40 grid, subtract top and left padding, clamp to its final cell, and emit exact one-based cell 100,40. Every screen, cell, and padding field participates in the report boundary or coordinate result.

title: Prove rich presentation fidelity on attachment and reattachment
description:
Contract routing:
- Hardens ORB-C4 and ORB-C6.
- Preserves ORB-C1 through ORB-C3, ORB-C5, and ORB-C7.
- Changes no product feature or compatibility boundary unless the user separately approves it.

Prove complete canonical frames preserve the accepted rich visible terminal state across attachment and reattachment without a formatter bootstrap, raw-byte replica, or client-owned emulator.
design:
Run after semantic input and resize hardening. Record the Execution baseline and pass the Reference gate before code.

Required before code: exact libghostty-vt render, row, cell, grapheme, cursor, title, hyperlink, screen, and capability surfaces; and zmx restoration failures showing why formatted text is insufficient. FrankenTUI deterministic scene-transition checks are comparison only here. Reject TUI cells, formatted-ANSI restoration, dirty-row patches, and client terminal emulation.

Exercise primary and alternate screens, styled Unicode, combining and wide graphemes, resolved backgrounds, cursor shapes and visibility, title, hyperlinks, complete-frame revision order, coherent replacement on reattach, resize, and explicit unsupported capability reporting. Stop for graphics, effects, history, patches, protocol revision, dependency, or Venus correction.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Complete frames preserve accepted styled graphemes, combining and wide-cell roles, resolved colors, cursor, title, hyperlinks, screen state, and explicit capabilities.
2. Attachment and reattachment materialize one coherent complete state followed by strictly ordered revisions with no stale final presentation.
3. Alternate-screen transitions and resize remain semantically equivalent without formatter restoration, raw PTY replay, or a client terminal emulator.
4. Supported rich state is never silently collapsed to plain text, and unsupported graphics or effects remain explicit rather than partially invented.
5. Focused checks use canonical frames and authoritative state and distinguish protocol fidelity from native Venus rendering quality.
6. Orbit is the sole code owner; any Venus or boundary defect is routed separately with exact revisions and compatibility order.
7. Closure advances or explicitly downgrades ORB-C4 and ORB-C6 at an exact proof revision, regression-checks preserved contracts, and records portability, dependency footprint, LOC, exact verification, and remaining capability gaps.
notes:
Accepted state

Ownership and code shape: Orbit remains the sole terminal-state and presentation owner. ORBF v1, the extractor, runtime, protocol, and client boundary require no production change. The existing real_pty_reattach_converges_through_complete_ordered_frames test is the single proof owner.

The proof drives one live shell into a resized 80x30 alternate screen and checks the canonical frame for exact default and palette colors; hyperlink; RGB foreground, resolved background, underline color, bold, italic, faint, blink, inverse, invisible, strike, overline, curly underline, and protection; a combining grapheme; wide head and spacer-tail roles; a background-only erased cell; hidden steady-underline cursor state; title; working directory; active screen; hyperlink support; and explicit absence of Kitty graphics. A second client receives a byte-decoded frame exactly equal to that complete rich revision. After the deterministic release changes authoritative state, the next attached initial frame is strictly newer than the rich revision; any following frames are also strictly ordered. The pressure phase preserves final primary-screen convergence after a slow client, semantic interrupt, split CSI, UTF-8, and APC input.

Simplification disposition: keep the single real-pipeline proof. Helpers, expected-frame fixtures, split matrices, and weaker aggregate assertions add machinery or lose field-level evidence without removing an owned concept. No production refactor is justified.

Rejected shapes remain formatter restoration, raw PTY replay, client terminal emulation, a second schema, graphical Venus claims, graphics or effects invention, history, patches, protocol revision, dependencies, and additional test matrices.

Proof lifecycle: the user accepted proof-bearing commit 847cab1ca37495c5cd45454623bd81909b488564. ORB-C4 and ORB-C6 advance to that immutable revision in docs/CONTRACTS.md. ORB-C1 through ORB-C3, ORB-C5, and ORB-C7 are preserved by unchanged production code and the passing canonical suite.

Dependencies and LOC: Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, and docs/CRATES.md are unchanged; the ten-package normal graph remains. Product Rust source and tests are 6,027 lines, up 70 test-only lines; governance is 765; total owned Rust is 6,792. No production LOC changed.

title: Measure the accepted Orbit-Venus boundary under real workloads
description: This is the final no-code acceptance slice for orb-bi4.5. It changes no product contract. Consume the exact accepted Orbit and Venus proofs and measure the real one-client boundary under representative terminal workloads. Route every confirmed defect to its single owning repository and Bead instead of repairing it inside this measurement run.
design:
Run only after transport pressure, lifecycle, and terminal-semantic hardening close. Pin the exact ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 and VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 proof revisions being exercised.

Before the first workload run, record the exact machine, display stack, window and grid size, commands, sampling method, and explicit numeric pass/fail ceilings. The envelope must cover p50 and p95 input-to-present latency when externally observable, idle CPU and RSS, sustained-output CPU and RSS, extraction time, encoded bytes per frame and per second, queue replacement, Venus apply or rebuild time, resize-storm convergence, and final-state convergence. title: Dogfood Venus and Orbit through a minimum Eon path
description:
Track Orbit-side acceptance of the smallest user-activated Eon dogfood path over exact Eon, Orbit and Venus revisions after the hardened live-presentation boundary and minimum native history, scrolling, selection and copy baseline are accepted.

The accepted workload includes one real coding-agent CLI performing bounded useful work as an ordinary PTY process. This Bead proves only whether Orbit process lifetime and coherent Venus reattachment materially help that workflow. It creates no agent protocol, provider integration, observer, semantic status model, Eon implementation, package metadata or product support claim.

Eon owns integration code and workspace policy in the separate eon repository. Orbit owns terminal-session and process lifetime, authoritative live state, retained history, viewport, selection and copy text. Venus owns native frame materialization, gesture capture, accessibility and clipboard side effects. Failures return to exactly one owner. Nova remains unchanged.
design:
Begin only after orb-bi4.5 and its performance decision are accepted, orb-j0m closes with exact Orbit and Venus native-history proofs, and the user activates Eon through eon-68v. eon-omq owns the component manifest and eon-ax4 owns Nix-only implementation and dogfood.

Dogfood ordinary shell, Neovim, Yazi, a full-screen TUI, long output and one selected current coding-agent CLI on a bounded real task in a disposable or explicitly chosen repository/worktree. Record the exact CLI identity and mode without publishing credentials, private prompts or sensitive terminal output. Disconnect or exit Venus while the agent task remains active; verify Orbit, the PTY and agent process survive; reattach coherently; continue user interaction; and observe a completion or failure.

This pre-graduation agent workload does not require an Eon AgentRun model. It must distinguish authoritative process/terminal lifecycle from semantic agent state. Without provider-authored signals, working, blocked, waiting, completed and failed remain unknown rather than inferred from titles, output text, timing or process names.

Compare the pair with the current Nova Mars and Zellij path on identical named conditions. Inspect exact current Herdr and VS Code Agent Host mechanisms as comparison evidence for client-independent agent work, not as dependencies or inherited feature scope. Record friction against the owning contract rather than widening Orbit, Venus or Eon.

Separate repositories remain deliberate boundaries whose coordination cost is measured at graduation.

7. One real coding-agent CLI at an exact recorded version performs a bounded useful task. Venus disconnects or exits while it remains active; Orbit, the PTY and agent process survive; restarted Venus coherently reattaches; user interaction continues; and a completion or failure is observed.
8. Agent evidence records no credentials or sensitive content and creates no provider support claim, provider-state model, observer, control surface or new protocol.
9. Evidence distinguishes process lifecycle from semantic agent state. Missing provider-authored state is reported as unknown; terminal text, titles, timing and process names are not authoritative status.
10. Native history scrolling, key return to live, Unicode and wrapped-row selection, copy, resize and reflow, alternate screen, pruning, stale revisions, Venus restart and bounded failures work through accepted contracts.
11. Comparable startup, high-output, idle-resource, interaction, history, copy, detach, reattach and agent-workflow observations use identical named conditions where a performance claim is made.
12. Ownership review confirms Eon contains policy and adapters only, Orbit remains terminal authority and Venus remains native presentation and interaction owner.
13. Every failure routes to an EON-C, VEN-C or ORB-C owner with exact compatible or breaking update order rather than a silent adapter.
14. Any Eon process or package probe proves only Eon launch, environment, ordering, packaging, versions or failure policy; it cannot advance Orbit or Venus proof.
15. Accepted user-visible integration behavior updates affected changelogs; candidate observations and planning do not.
16. Search, effects, semantic regions, agent observation, AgentRun state, machine-readable agent actions, multiple sessions, layouts, panes, plugins, remote access, restart persistence and direct distribution remain excluded.

title: Choose post-graduation Eon, Venus, and Orbit ownership boundaries
description:
After a go in orb-bi4.8, choose exactly one post-graduation implementation frontier and its cross-repository order. Preserve Orbit as generic terminal-session authority, Venus as native materializer and interaction owner, and Eon as agent-first workspace, product policy, orchestration, composition and distribution owner. On a no-go, close this Bead as not applicable.

Product direction:
Agents are strategically central to Eon. The user selected eon-pxn as the single post-graduation implementation frontier: an Eon-owned workspace model that treats AgentRun as explicit product identity and maps it to repositories or worktrees, provider identities, services, artifacts, execution targets and independent Orbit sessions. Its user-selected first native topology is a fixed two-axis surface: horizontal tabs and a visual vertical accordion pane stack with direct directional traversal and no virtual pane picker. This decision establishes ownership and order without activating implementation or another frontier.

Narrow-waist rule:
1. Keep an agent independent from a pane, PTY, process, Orbit session, provider thread and Venus view.
2. Keep process and terminal truth in Orbit, provider-native semantic evidence in an explicit integration, normalized AgentRun and attention policy in Eon, and native presentation in Venus.
3. For cross-boundary behavior compare no protocol change, an existing bounded plane and the smallest explicit extension in that order.
4. Keep snapshots or patches, history, effects, resources, actions, agent observation and product control as distinct responsibilities.
5. Every extension names one benefit, owner, consumer, numeric bounds, authorization, cancellation, compatibility, portability, proof and total LOC/runtime cost.
6. Keep exact-revision lockstep while Orbit and Venus are the only accepted pair. Add no public protocol, shared schema repository, compatibility window, generalized negotiation, plugin ABI or provider framework without an independently approved need.
7. Accept one vertical slice before another. Reopen architecture rather than accumulate adapters when coordination or duplicated truth becomes disproportionate.
design:
Current ownership:
- Orbit owns PTYs, terminal state, terminal viewport, selection, copy text, process/session lifetime and generic terminal identity.
- Venus owns frame materialization, native gesture collection, window geometry, focus, accessibility and platform clipboard or launch side effects. It owns no terminal viewport or history truth.
- Eon owns workspace topology and product policy: repositories or worktrees, AgentRuns, services, artifacts, execution-target references, launch and resume policy, secrets policy, component relationships and mappings to Orbit session identities.

Agent state remains source-aware. Orbit can prove process/session lifecycle, not provider intent. Provider semantic state is accepted only from an explicit integration. Eon may compute attention from fresh accepted evidence and must show unknown when semantic evidence is absent. Venus displays Eon state without scraping terminal content.

The first agent-workspace slice should compare no machine-readable surface with a deterministic local CLI or existing local socket for stable-ID list, tab and pane creation, directional or identity focus, attach, start, wait, explicit stop, and view removal distinct from session termination. Bounded terminal observation remains a separate read-only capability owned through orb-p92. MCP may later adapt accepted Eon actions; it is not the first protocol, plugin system or authorization owner.

For eon-pxn, the chosen bounded Eon workspace composes multiple independent one-session Orbit endpoints as one product slice: Eon owns horizontal-tab and per-tab vertical-pane order, Venus materializes a visual accordion with one expanded pane and persistent collapsed headers, and direct workspace commands traverse tabs left or right and panes up or down without a picker. This does not authorize an Orbit multi-session process or give Orbit layout ownership.

Decide an Orbit process that hosts multiple sessions separately from Eon workspace topology, restart recovery separately from detach, remote terminal transport separately from web/mobile presentation, and remote environment orchestration separately from all three. Effects, search, semantic regions, observation and graphics remain separate candidates. Select exactly one frontier.

Accepted decision and update order:
1. Activate the minimum eon-pxn Eon owner for stable tab and pane identities, ordered topology, independent Orbit-session mappings, and only the semantic actions required by that topology.
2. Activate a separate Eon-owned managed interactive-environment child under eon-pxn. Eon owns its selected components, exact identities, private configuration, command projection, and product defaults; the tools retain native behavior and schema ownership.
3. Activate the Venus consumer for opaque horizontal tabs and the one-expanded vertical accordion. Orbit remains unchanged unless an exact owner-contract gap is found.
4. Prove the cross-repository dogfood workspace.
5. Only after the opaque workspace passes, separately activate the minimum Venus appearance capability for Eon-owned font, theme, bell, and default-background opacity policy.

The full managed-environment decision lives in eon-pxn. Orbit only launches the exact selected argv and retains process, PTY, terminal, and session authority; it does not own Nushell, prompt, editor, file-manager, Git UI, PATH, alias, theme, font, bell, or opacity policy. Opaque tabs do not wait for a general configuration system, plugin mechanism, observation plane, effects framework, remote support, or native Eon editor. A missing prerequisite pauses the frontier at its real owner rather than inviting a Venus or Orbit workaround.
acceptance_criteria:
1. orb-bi4.8 records the graduation decision first.
2. After a go, every proposed expansion receives accept, reject or defer with one repository owner.
3. eon-pxn is the selected single next frontier because agents are strategically central to Eon. Its accepted first topology is horizontal tabs plus per-tab visual vertical accordion panes, one expanded pane at a time, direct directional traversal and no ordinary vertical pane picker.
4. The selected agent-workspace contract keeps AgentRun distinct from pane, process, PTY, Orbit session, provider thread and Venus view.
5. Ownership preserves Orbit terminal, viewport, selection and copy authority; Venus native presentation and interaction; and Eon workspace, AgentRun, action and attention policy without duplicate truth.
6. Process lifecycle, provider semantic state and Eon attention state have explicit separate sources. Unknown semantic state is never guessed from terminal output, titles, timing or process names.
7. Any first Eon action surface compares no API with a minimal deterministic local CLI or existing socket for stable-ID list, tab and pane creation, directional or identity focus, attach, start, wait, explicit stop, and view removal distinct from session termination. It separates read-only observation from mutating actions; MCP, plugins, pane pickers, raw terminal control and provider-specific actions remain separate decisions.
8. Eon composition of multiple independent one-session Orbit endpoints and its bounded horizontal-tab plus visual-accordion topology travel together under eon-pxn. An Orbit process hosting multiple sessions, simultaneous expanded panes, arbitrary or durable layouts, virtual pane pickers, floating terminal popups, restart recovery, state patches, effects, search, semantic regions, observation, graphics, remote attachment, web/mobile clients and remote machines remain separately decidable slices.
9. Each accepted responsibility defines its user contract, known consumers, exact update order, authorization, bounds, cancellation, proof, portability, LOC and maintenance before implementation planning.
10. Exactly one implementation frontier is selected; all others remain deferred.
11. Separate repositories remain the default. A monorepo, shared schema repository, compatibility layer, new protocol owner or provider framework requires explicit user approval.
12. Eon and Nova remain independent.
13. On a no-go, this Bead closes as not applicable without speculative cleanup or planning scope.
14. The selected implementation order is the minimum Eon topology and action owner; a separate Eon-managed interactive-environment child; the Venus opaque horizontal-tab and one-expanded vertical-accordion consumer; cross-repository dogfood acceptance; and only then a separately approved Venus appearance child. Broader AgentRun/provider semantics, declarative profiles, terminal observation, MCP, plugins, isolation, generalized APIs, and effects remain outside the first workspace slice unless a required owner-contract gap blocks it.
15. eon-pxn is the sole owner of the accepted managed-environment details and Eon product defaults. Orbit receives exact launch inputs but gains no shell, tool, PATH, configuration, font, theme, bell, or opacity policy.
16. Tabs and accordion panes prove opaque composition first. Default-background opacity is later Venus capability work under a separately approved VEN contract, while the 0.92 product default and immediate 1.0 override remain Eon policy. A missing prerequisite returns to its owning repository before the frontier continues.
notes:
Selected frontier: P1 Eon agent-first workspace eon-pxn. Deferred alternatives remain P1 phased read-only agent observation orb-p92; P1 Orbit effects separation orb-ll1; P2 search orb-qcc; P2 semantic command regions orb-3gf; P3 graphics orb-j2i; P1 Venus hyperlink interaction; and P2 Venus structured accessibility. This decision activates no parallel implementation.

At activation, eon-pxn creates separate Eon owner, any required Orbit owner, Venus consumer and acceptance children. No implementation children are created by this planning correction.

User topology decision on 2026-08-07: keep the first workspace deliberately two-axis and visible. Tabs traverse horizontally; panes form a visual vertical accordion with one expanded session and bounded persistent headers. Ordinary up or down pane traversal does not open a picker. This is Eon/Venus product topology over independent Orbit sessions, not an Orbit layout or multi-session contract.

Exact current Herdr, Amp Orbs and VS Code Agent Host material informs agent-workspace and client-independent execution mechanisms only. Canario remains the compact workspace cost comparator. No reference is a dependency or compatibility target.

First-slice sequencing clarification (2026-08-08): eon-pxn is the product frontier. Eon first owns stable tab and pane identities, ordering, independent Orbit-session mappings, and only the semantic actions required by the slice; a separate Eon child proves the managed interactive environment; Venus then materializes opaque horizontal tabs and the visual accordion; cross-repository dogfood accepts the result. Do not build the complete AgentRun/provider model, declarative profile, observation, extension, isolation, or generalized API horizon before this workspace proof, and do not let Venus compensate for a missing Eon contract.

Decision completed by user on 2026-08-08: select eon-pxn and its owner-first order. The Eon topology/action owner precedes the separately scoped managed interactive environment; Venus then consumes the topology as opaque tabs and accordion panes; cross-repository dogfood follows; appearance comes later. eon-pxn records the accepted Nushell, Starship, Zoxide, Helix, Yazi, LazyGit, managed-command, private-PATH, manifest, theme, font, bell, and opacity policy. Nova revision `37f36efcabf16c41d03e182917926e7b8e56139c` is comparison evidence for that Eon-owned plan only. Carapace, automatic Direnv or Mise activation, command-alias configuration, cursor effects, general configuration, plugins, observation, and generalized APIs stay deferred. No implementation child or product contract is created by this closure.

Future Eon Web direction selected by the user on 2026-08-10: use a TypeScript browser shell, compile the canonical Rust Orbit protocol decoder and client-state reducer to WebAssembly, and use Effect as the default browser-side lifecycle runtime for typed transport failures, resource scopes, cancellation, bounded concurrency and streams, scheduling, reconnect, and deterministic substitution in tests. Plain browser code retains DOM, ARIA, input, clipboard, rendering, and PWA ownership. Effect does not decode ORBF or ORBS, own terminal state, render the terminal, define remote authorization, or become an Eon-wide plugin or schema framework. Agent-assisted development velocity is an accepted reason not to reject the stronger lifecycle model merely for unfamiliar syntax, learning cost, or initial implementation effort; exact ownership, lifecycle correctness, security, dependency health, bundle and runtime cost, and replacement cost still govern adoption. This selects the future default shape but activates no web contract, remote transport, repository, dependency, or implementation.

title: Decide whether Venus and Orbit earn Eon graduation
description:
Decision gate: decide whether the proven Venus and Orbit pair earns the Eon implementation frontier after hardening, minimum native history, scrolling, selection and copy, and fresh Eon dogfood that includes one real coding-agent lifecycle. This Bead changes no runtime contract or implementation.

Required evidence:

- The accepted workload envelope and the native-history end-to-end LOC, latency, CPU, memory, request, failure-state and compatibility evidence.
- Fresh native dogfood demonstrating whether client-independent process lifetime, coherent reattachment, one terminal authority and explicit failure ownership are materially valuable for ordinary terminal work and for one bounded real coding-agent task.
- A refreshed Canario comparison with separate distribution and mechanism evidence. Use `canarioterm/releases` commit `fcadcfeea7e337114d28beec0e0cbe89493a654d` and release `v2026.08.07.15`, built from private revision `canario@af91699`, for distribution evidence. Use Rio `ff8efcc4ad0359889de44b1baacea7014cdada30`, the final public Canario tree before extraction commit `e69b5fffef25abd5e649bf4ac205636551e54482`, for inspectable same-process lifetime and restoration mechanisms. Treat current private internals as unknown.
- Exact current Herdr evidence for durable agent terminals and client-independent work. Compare mechanisms and proved user contracts. Adoption, screenshots, commit counts and feature breadth carry no decision weight.

Protocol-gravity falsification:
Measure the full cost of ordinary history, scrolling, selection and copy across the boundary: owned code, protocol messages and bounds, repositories, handoffs, compatibility, failure states and runtime cost. Compare that tax with demonstrated process survival, independent client failure, replaceable clients and structured authority. Agent value receives credit only for the exact real workload completed in orb-bi4.6. Do not credit speculative observer, AgentRun, remote, multiplayer, web, plugin, provider integration or restart-persistence value.

Decision rule:
- Go only if dogfood makes the accepted lifetime and authority benefits materially useful, including the real agent task, and the cross-boundary cost remains proportionate and maintainable.
- No-go if an integrated shape satisfies the chosen contract more simply, Venus reconstructs Orbit truth, ordinary capabilities require disproportionate protocol ceremony, or agent benefit appears only in unimplemented future surfaces.
- A no-go records the smallest rollback or simplification boundary and implements nothing.
design:
Compare Venus and Orbit with the current Mars and Zellij path, Mars Next, Canario, zmx, justerm-core and Herdr. Separate Canario distribution evidence at `canarioterm/releases` `fcadcfeea7e337114d28beec0e0cbe89493a654d` and `v2026.08.07.15` from mechanism evidence in the final public Rio tree `ff8efcc4ad0359889de44b1baacea7014cdada30`. Keep component references distinct from competing architectures.

Judge two demonstrated questions separately:
1. Is the one-authority structured terminal path coherent and worth its three-repository and protocol cost for ordinary terminal behavior?
2. Does a real coding-agent process materially benefit from surviving Venus loss and coherent reattachment without claiming any unimplemented agent-state, workspace, observer, control, remote or restore feature?

The real agent run is an ordinary PTY process. Graduation does not define AgentRun, provider status or an agent API. It determines whether the foundation improves the selected agent workflow enough to justify continuing toward the separately planned Eon agent-first workspace.

A go accepts Venus and Orbit as the Eon foundation and unblocks orb-bi4.7. It does not modify Nova, activate workspace or agent features, promote channels, add repositories, create compatibility windows or implement follow-up scope. A no-go records retained evidence and the user-selected retain or delete boundary.

Venus materializes frames, captures native input, exposes accessibility and clipboard effects, and owns no PTY or terminal model.
- Eon manifest proof `c9e898c9ff889c2be4d4381a20676291bab65b49` pins Orbit `00b1363` and Venus `2d36c72`. EON-C1 proof `712c0834691c58b07e56494de25f98670b6a882e` and EON-C2 through EON-C4 composition proof `eae70e8d3ed4348b389f320dfd49d7db29478546` establish the accepted Nix-only Linux composition. EON-C5 through EON-C7 remain planned distribution work and carry no foundation correctness claim.
- The owner-first ORBS v2 change landed in Orbit, then Venus pinned the exact revision, then Eon pinned the accepted pair. No adapter, duplicate schema, feature probe, dual decoder or compatibility window exists.

Demonstrated value

Closed orb-bi4.6 consumed a fresh Eon run with Codex CLI 0.147.0 in a disposable Rust repository. Venus exited while Codex was active. Eon, Orbit, the PTY and Codex survived; `eon attach` opened a new Venus against the same session; the task completed; and independent format, test and Clippy checks passed. Provider semantic state remained unknown. The same component pair exercised 3,000 history rows, rapid wheel input, return to live, wrapped Unicode, wide-grapheme selection and copy, resize and reflow, Helix, Neovim, Yazi keyboard and application mouse, DEC 1007, output pressure, client loss and coherent reattachment.

The corrected sustained-output envelope passed at combined CPU p95 167 percent under the declared 200 percent ceiling, peak combined RSS 55.3 MiB and final convergence 13.6 ms. The native history proof completed 32 synchronous wheel round trips in 39.620976 ms with a 12,809-byte complete ORBS frame. The real-pair lifecycle proof observed coherent reattachment in 122 ms. These measurements retain their named workloads and do not become broad performance claims.

ORBF v1 carries styled graphemes, colors, cursor, title, working directory, hyperlinks, active-screen identity and explicit capability flags. Orbit owns retained history, viewport, selection and copy; Venus never reconstructs terminal state from text or PTY bytes. The accepted capability set preserves rich state without a visible-screen or text-grid ceiling. Kitty graphics remain declared unsupported.

Protocol and ownership cost

Orbit added 57 production and 370 test lines for authoritative viewport behavior. Selection and copy raised product Rust and tests from 6,454 to 7,161 lines, a further 707 lines. Current Orbit accounting is 7,183 product Rust lines, 765 governance Rust lines and two terminfo lines. The dependency-free `orbit-protocol` package owns 3,100 Rust lines, including 2,131 production and 969 test lines.

The accepted Venus history, selection, copy and accessibility slice changed 835 net Rust lines from its pre-slice baseline and added arboard 3.6.1 behind the native clipboard seam. Arboard required 15 Venus production lines and 12 all-target lock packages. Current Venus accounting is 4,359 Rust source lines, 363 integration-test lines and 5,301 tracked handwritten lines. Eon keeps one component manifest and launch owner; its current scorecard includes 1,026 Rust source and test lines.

At the exact comparison revisions, Eon, Orbit and Venus contain about 12,931 tracked Rust lines across their scorecards. Nova `cf313431ca0b08352b0a5b4b0beb2341aee5568a`, Mars `2b63717135a72ef330d8c2da8ca4cde59c22d739` and Yazelix Zellij `bbccdea6eda81f314151160f9b3f8882a26478ec` contain about 521,170 tracked Rust lines. These raw maintenance surfaces do not equate feature sets, but the gap supports the smaller ownership conclusion. Nova remains an independent product because Eon still excludes its layouts, plugins and multi-session workspace behavior.

Comparator result

Canario publishes builds through `canarioterm/releases` commit `fcadcfeea7e337114d28beec0e0cbe89493a654d`; release `v2026.08.07.15` records private source `canario@af91699`. Current private internals remain unknown. Rio `ff8efcc4ad0359889de44b1baacea7014cdada30`, the final public tree before extraction `e69b5fffef25abd5e649bf4ac205636551e54482`, remains the inspectable integrated comparator. It keeps PTYs in the application, restarts shells and restores layout, CWD, title and text scrollback. That shape has lower protocol cost but fails the selected live-process survival contract.

Herdr main `3a76fea2d858a7a5ef58615f1cc9aabaa30b80ee` and stable release `v0.8.0` publish a server/client contract for durable agent terminals and transient clients. Herdr also owns workspaces, multiple panes, restart restoration, remote attachment, agent heuristics, integrations, plugins and an agent API. Graduation accepts its process-continuity lesson and gives zero credit to those broader surfaces.

The Canario integrated shape cannot satisfy ORB-C1, and Herdr corroborates the value of a separate durable terminal owner. Neither reference justifies compatibility or adoption. Complete frames remain accepted because the measured envelope passed; patches, dirty-row extraction and a second renderer remain deferred.

Risks and limits

The audit found one approved protocol exception: orb-bi4.2 comment 14 records the user's 2026-08-04 one-time authorization to reconstruct baseline, reference and crate-gate evidence after those timing rules were adopted during the candidate. The exception applies only to orb-bi4.2, does not claim the records predated implementation, and does not extend to another Bead. Later accepted proofs reran the canonical checks.

No known P0 or P1 correctness blocker remains. Open or deferred P1 items are decision or feature scope: orb-bi4.7, agent observation, ordered effects, Venus hyperlinks and Eon workspace planning. Linux/Nix and Xwayland carry the accepted proof. macOS, native Wayland quality, candidate-list IME quality, proprietary NVIDIA packaging, direct distribution and restart persistence remain unproved. One synthetic wheel delta of 80 disconnected Venus, while representative rapid unit input passed and reattachment recovered. Optional emoji and Yazi icons showed fallback boxes. Search, effects, graphics, richer selection, multiple sessions, layouts, remote transport, web and mobile remain separate decisions.

The selected dependency cost remains material: libghostty-vt 0.2.1 builds pinned Ghostty `a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083` through Zig, the source checkout measured about 155 MiB, Venus carries a native GPU, shaping and accessibility stack, and the Eon Nix closure is about 1.46 GiB. Exact lockstep across three repositories remains a maintenance cost. Dogfood, bounded failure ownership and the smaller maintenance surface justify that cost at this stage.

Two nonblocking metadata discrepancies remain outside this authorized planning-only run: the Orbit crate index retains an obsolete sentence that Venus still consumes ORBS v1 until `ven-4sn`, and Venus VEN-C3/VEN-C4 rows retain historical partial-ORB-C7 wording against their original consumed proof despite the current Eon pair pinning proved ORB-C7. The canonical current consumer relationship in Orbit and Eon contract indexes is correct.

Decision consequence

Graduation unblocks orb-bi4.7 to choose exactly one post-graduation frontier. This run creates no implementation bead, starts no frontier, changes no changelog and does not promote a distribution channel. Nova remains unchanged.
close_reason: GO at 80 percent confidence: accepted Orbit, Venus, and Eon proofs plus real Codex dogfood demonstrate useful process survival and coherent terminal authority at proportionate measured cost; orb-bi4.7 may select one frontier.

title: Extract the canonical ORBF v1 codec for Venus
description: Create the smallest Orbit-owned, platform-neutral Rust protocol surface that lets Orbit and Venus consume one canonical ORBF v1 interpretation at exact revisions without changing the accepted wire contract.
design: Add one dependency-free orbit-protocol package inside the Orbit workspace. It owns ORBF v1 version and bounds, canonical frame data, bounded decode and validation, byte encoding, and complete-frame revision reduction. The existing Orbit server consumes the package while libghostty extraction remains in Orbit; Venus later consumes the exact same package from a pinned Orbit Git revision. Preserve ORB-C4, ORB-C6, and ORB-C7 behavior and byte compatibility. Do not add a new wire version, public trace format, fourth repository, crates.io publication, renderer, raw PTY path, terminal state, schema generator, or external dependency.
acceptance_criteria:
1. An Execution baseline records current HEAD, policy hash, Bead revision, ORB-C4/ORB-C6/ORB-C7 routing, intended surfaces, dirty paths, and session identity.
2. A pre-code Reference gate inspects the accepted Orbit proof and every required exact-revision source; a package/dependency gate records the user-approved ownership choice before manifest edits.
3. One platform-neutral dependency-free orbit-protocol workspace package owns ORBF v1 constants, bounds, frame representation, bounded decode/validation, encoding, and strict complete-frame revision reduction.
4. Orbit presentation extraction uses that package and emits byte-compatible frames without changing ORB-C4 or ORB-C6 behavior.
5. Decoder checks reject bad magic, unsupported versions, truncation, trailing bytes, invalid tags/flags/dimensions, allocation-hostile lengths, and stale or regressing revisions within explicit bounds.
6. A canonical corpus generated by Orbit round-trips through the package and includes styled Unicode/graphemes, cursor, alternate screen, title, working directory, hyperlinks, and declared unsupported graphics.
7. The package is consumable from the exact Orbit Git revision without compiling Orbit PTY, libc, libghostty, or governance owners.
8. No external crate, generated mirror, adapter, compatibility window, trace format, command, or additional binary is added.
9. Canonical Rust checks and governance pass; owned LOC, package/dependency footprint, byte compatibility, portability disposition, and remaining gaps are recorded.
10. Touched proved contracts remain partial until an accepted proof-bearing commit, then ORB-C4 and ORB-C6 advance to that exact revision; ORB-C7 remains honestly partial unless its full hardening gap is closed.
notes: User approval on 2026-08-04 explicitly selected the Orbit-owned protocol package and a narrowly scoped implementation Bead after ven-upt.1 reported the missing canonical consumer surface. This Bead preserves existing product contracts; it does not activate Venus graphical implementation.
close_reason: Accepted canonical ORBF v1 codec proof at 6e53fedb97f764f3683c83edcd9a5227b8f56e56.
