title: Qualify rio-vt as a disposable Orbit engine candidate
description:
## Why

The user selected a bounded rio-vt experiment because its durable evidence is useful whether rio-vt passes, partially fits, or fails. Orbit currently depends on libghostty-vt 0.2.1 and Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083. rio-vt may offer lower Rust-side integration friction, more direct terminal-state access, easier Orbit-specific experimentation, and a more approachable basis if Yazelix ever chooses to own a terminal engine. It may instead prove that libghostty's mature terminal semantics and cleaner embedding boundary outweigh Zig and FFI cost.

This task qualifies one exact rio-vt revision against the completed Orbit conformance corpus and records a decision-quality gap matrix. It does not replace libghostty, add a supported engine, or create a permanent dual-engine architecture.

Contract routing:
- Changes no product behavior, ORB-C contract, wire compatibility, proof status, or supported dependency.
- Consumes the exact completed orb-8s0 corpus and evaluates preservation of ORB-C2, ORB-C4, ORB-C5, ORB-C6, ORB-C8, and ORB-C9.
- A candidate pass cannot promote or replace an accepted proof. Adoption requires a separate explicit user decision, contract routing, dependency gate, implementation Bead, and proof lifecycle.

## Evidence

- docs/CRATES.md records libghostty-vt 0.2.1 as the selected authoritative engine, its existing ten-package Rust graph, Ghostty source and Zig build cost, and rio-vt as an unselected replacement candidate.
- docs/REFERENCES.md:188-201 routes rio-vt commit 3e41b8b19a1cad9cd9bdfc8f7900cf61ce5a9098 as the strongest Rust-native alternative and rejects librio as a substitute for Orbit's detach boundary.
- rio-vt/Cargo.toml:18-39 keeps corcovado, teletypewriter, simdutf, configuration/search support, and other dependencies non-optional on the normal non-Wasm path. simdutf 0.7.0 builds bundled C++ through cc, so current rio-vt is Cargo-managed but not a strictly Rust-source-only dependency graph.
- rio-vt/src/event/mod.rs:128-288 mixes terminal effects and PTY replies with Rio application commands such as native tabs, fullscreen, quake mode, configuration, window creation, and shutdown.
- rio-vt/src/crosswords/mod.rs:423-463 exposes direct grid, selection, color, title, graphics, cursor, route, working-directory, user-variable, and renderer-notification state. This is powerful for experimentation but creates coupling and API-stability risk.
- rio-vt/README.md:98-127 still requires an EventListener::event method removed from the actual trait at rio-vt/src/event/mod.rs:413-421, confirming churn in the newly extracted embedding surface.
- librio/src/lib.rs:230-335 owns a PTY, terminal machine, I/O thread, and process lifecycle. That shape violates Orbit's sole PTY and owner-loop authority and is excluded.
- include/ghostty/vt/terminal.h:20-109 exposes an opaque caller-driven terminal with synchronous effects and no required PTY, renderer, timer, or background-thread ownership, which currently fits Orbit's boundary.
- At Rio commit 3e41b8b, rio-vt contains about 27,055 Rust code lines and 442 #[test] functions. Its standalone extraction began at a0a7a0e05 on 2026-07-26 and received 43 follow-up commits by the inspected 2026-08-05 revision. The underlying Rio terminal code predates the extraction; the embeddable public seam is new.
- At Ghostty a887df42, src/terminal contains about 89,650 Zig code lines, 2,376 Zig tests, and a substantial parser/OSC fuzz corpus. These counts are maintenance evidence, not directly comparable correctness scores.

## Scope

In scope:
- Qualify one exact rio-vt revision, beginning with 3e41b8b19a1cad9cd9bdfc8f7900cf61ce5a9098 unless activation records a newer exact release and preserves comparison with this baseline.
- Feed the orb-8s0 deterministic stimuli into rio-vt and translate only Orbit-owned semantic observations needed by the corpus.
- Measure corpus results, adapter LOC and coupling, dependencies and source languages, build and offline/Nix implications, focused engine throughput and memory under one identical correctness-checked workload, and gaps in state, input, effects, history, selection, graphics, and lifecycle integration.
- Compare four long-term shapes: retain libghostty; retain rio-vt as a benchmark only; pursue bounded upstream rio-vt cleanup then requalify; or recommend a separate adoption/fork decision.
- Preserve exact commands, source identities, adapter patch or recipe, raw measurements, classifications, and negative results as Bead evidence.

Out of scope:
- Using librio, Sugarloaf, Canario, Rio's PTY/event loop/windowing, or another renderer.
- Editing production Orbit code, replacing libghostty, changing Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock without the required gate and user approval, changing ORBS/ORBF, adding a runtime engine trait or feature flag, supporting two engines, publishing a trace format, creating a repository, or shipping candidate code.
- Forking Rio or Ghostty, implementing orbit-vt, upstream issues or pull requests, terminal feature fixes, Venus rendering, end-to-end product benchmarking, or compatibility claims.

## Acceptance Criteria

The canonical criteria are stored in this Bead's `acceptance_criteria` field.
design:
## Implementation Notes

1. Begin only after orb-8s0 is closed with an exact accepted corpus revision and documented command. Claim this Bead and record its Execution baseline before any proof-code, test, manifest, or fixture edit.
2. Complete the Reference gate before proof code. Required: exact accepted Orbit contracts and corpus; rio-vt and librio at 3e41b8b19a1cad9cd9bdfc8f7900cf61ce5a9098; pinned libghostty-vt 0.2.1, libghostty-vt-sys 0.2.1, Ghostty a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083, and their relevant render/effect/input/test surfaces. Rio application, librio PTY, Sugarloaf, and Canario behavior are comparison or rejected scope, not inherited architecture.
3. Pass the Crate gate before any tracked manifest edit. Compare: source-only analysis; a disposable out-of-tree Cargo adapter; the smallest separately approved tracked non-product spike; and no experiment. Default to the out-of-tree adapter. If reproducibility cannot be retained through exact commands and a bounded patch/recipe, stop for user approval before adding a tracked package or workspace member.
4. Use rio-vt directly. Orbit remains the conceptual owner of PTY bytes, terminal-generated reply routing, semantic inputs, presentation extraction, bounds, and lifecycle. Do not instantiate rio-vt performer::Machine or librio Surface.
5. Start with the smallest in-memory engine cases. Add a bounded real-PTY comparison only if a named corpus invariant cannot be evaluated without Orbit's PTY owner. Do not reproduce the broader dogfood or performance baselines.
6. Map every entry in the accepted corpus inventory before execution. Exercise every engine-applicable case. Exclude a case only when its invariant belongs to Orbit's PTY, transport, or lifecycle boundary rather than terminal-engine semantics, recording the exact owner and rationale. Classify each exercised case as pass, equivalent-but-different, missing public surface, unsupported feature, candidate defect, ambiguous expectation, or harness defect. Exact equality applies only to canonical Orbit outputs; do not make libghostty internals the oracle.
7. Inventory every rio-vt type and field the adapter touches. Classify each as stable public API, exposed implementation detail, Rio application coupling, PTY/event-loop coupling, native/C++ dependency, or candidate fork pressure.
8. Measure clean build inputs, Cargo packages, native code/toolchains, offline/Nix requirements, build time, artifact size, adapter code, and one focused identical engine workload. Performance evidence must use the same stimuli, environment, repetitions, correctness oracle, and report a distribution or bound. It cannot claim Venus or end-to-end latency.
9. Evaluate current capabilities explicitly: parser partials; primary/alternate state; pending wrap; Unicode and graphemes; styles/colors/hyperlinks; title/CWD; terminal replies and effects; semantic input; resize/reflow; viewport/history; selection/copy; search; graphics; damage; state export/import. Record that rio-vt's visible VT formatter is not exact checkpoint/restore unless independently disproved.
10. End with exactly one recommendation: reject and retain libghostty; retain rio-vt only as a recurring comparator; request a bounded upstream cleanup and requalify; or ask the user to authorize a separate dependency/fork/adoption decision. Do not implement the recommendation in this Bead.

## Verification

- The completed orb-8s0 command passes unchanged for the accepted libghostty baseline.
- The exact rio-vt adapter command accounts for the complete accepted inventory: it runs every engine-applicable case, records evidence-backed exclusions only for non-engine-owned cases, and emits the classified result table.
- Repeating deterministic cases produces identical results.
- Focused measurements retain their raw samples, environment, correctness result, and summary distribution or bound.
- If any tracked Eon Sessions surface is separately approved, cargo fmt --check, cargo check --locked, cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, repository governance checks, and git diff --check pass. Otherwise br lint, br sync --flush-only, evidence hashes, and git diff --check cover the planning/evidence surface.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if orb-8s0 lacks an engine-consumable case boundary; report the exact gap without rewriting that Bead in this run.
- Stop if the first useful candidate requires Orbit to surrender PTY, terminal-reply, protocol, lifecycle, or presentation authority.
- Stop if a maintained Rio fork or production abstraction is required before a meaningful corpus pass.
- Stop for explicit user approval before a repository manifest, tracked spike package, fork, binding extension, public artifact, or product contract change.
- Stop if a candidate result would be reported as exact checkpointing, compatibility, performance superiority, or production readiness without direct proof.
- A corpus mismatch is evidence, not authorization to fix Orbit, rio-vt, Ghostty, or libghostty in this task.

Portability disposition: neutral engine stimuli and observations; record Linux build/runtime evidence and macOS/Wasm credibility separately without making support claims.
acceptance_criteria:
1. orb-8s0 is closed first, and the experiment records its exact corpus revision, contract mapping, command, and accepted libghostty baseline.
2. The experiment pins exact rio-vt, Rio, libghostty-vt, libghostty-vt-sys, and Ghostty identities and records licenses, relevant API maturity, and any source drift from the planning evidence.
3. No product code, ORB-C contract, ORBS/ORBF value, accepted proof, supported engine, production manifest, package, runtime flag, or distribution surface changes.
4. rio-vt is exercised directly without librio, Sugarloaf, Rio windowing, performer::Machine, Rio-owned PTY lifecycle, or a second terminal authority.
5. Every case in the accepted corpus inventory is accounted for. Each engine-applicable case has one classified result: pass, equivalent-but-different, missing public surface, unsupported, candidate defect, ambiguous expectation, or harness defect. An exclusion names the exact non-engine contract owner and rationale. No libghostty-internal behavior is promoted into an Orbit contract.
6. Results cover the accepted engine-sensitive surfaces in ORB-C2, ORB-C4, ORB-C5, ORB-C6, ORB-C8, and ORB-C9, including parser splits, screen transitions, wrap, Unicode, rich cells, replies/effects, input, resize/reflow, viewport/history, selection/copy, and presentation extraction.
7. The report distinguishes current capabilities from fork possibilities. It states explicitly whether exact parser/terminal checkpoint export and import exists; visible-screen VT formatting alone does not qualify.
8. One dependency/build matrix records normal direct and transitive packages, optional features, source languages including simdutf C++, unsafe/native boundaries, MSRV, toolchains, offline/Nix inputs, build time, and artifact size for both candidate and accepted baseline under named conditions.
9. One ownership matrix records adapter LOC, every relied-on rio-vt public type/field, app and PTY coupling, APIs that would need upstream cleanup, APIs that would force a fork, and estimated removal/maintenance cost. Estimates are labeled and grounded in exact source.
10. One bounded identical engine workload records correctness, raw samples, environment, repetitions, and a distribution or bound for throughput and memory. It makes no Venus, visual-latency, whole-product, or universal performance claim and does not duplicate orb-1sd.
11. The durable evidence includes exact commands, adapter recipe or patch, raw-result locations or hashes, classified corpus table, source/contract identities, negative results, limitations, and confidence so rejection is as reusable as success.
12. Closure records exactly one outcome: retain libghostty and reject rio-vt; retain rio-vt only as a benchmark; request separately authorized upstream cleanup then requalify; or recommend a separate user decision about adoption or a stripped fork.

notes:
User decision on 2026-08-08: create this experiment because it yields useful durable evidence regardless of candidate outcome. The experiment's product is the corpus result, boundary audit, dependency/build measurement, and gap matrix; candidate adapter code is disposable unless a later explicit decision says otherwise.

The central hypothesis is not that rio-vt is a better terminal today. It is that rio-vt may be better raw material if Yazelix later chooses to own terminal semantics. libghostty remains the default production recommendation while this task is deferred.

Known planning conclusions to preserve:
- rio-vt, not librio, is the only relevant engine candidate for Orbit.
- Rust-native state access, customization, and forkability are rio-vt's plausible unique advantages.
- Current upstream rio-vt does not provide exact checkpoint/restore and is not strictly Rust-source-only because simdutf builds C++.
- libghostty currently has the cleaner Orbit embedding boundary and much deeper conformance/fuzz evidence.
- Direct grid access is both an advantage and a coupling hazard.
- A passing spike is insufficient to justify migration; an independently valuable product requirement or material lifecycle-cost reduction must justify adoption.

Dependency order: orb-8s0 blocks this task. No graduation dependency is modeled because qualification evidence is technically independent; if Orbit receives a no-go and is abandoned, close this task as not applicable.

Rejected alternatives: a librio spike, a permanent backend feature flag, a generic engine trait before a second accepted engine, adopting rio-vt for language aesthetics alone, starting orbit-vt from scratch before measured requirements, or forking before upstream-clean fit is tested.

Planning estimate: effort M, 480 minutes. Implementation risk LOW because production remains untouched; interpretation risk MEDIUM due legitimate terminal-semantic differences; strategic risk HIGH if disposable code is allowed to become a maintained second backend.

title: Reconcile Orbit docs with Venus ORBS v3 adoption
description:
## Contract routing

This is a documentation reconciliation Bead. It changes no ORB product contract, wire behavior, implementation, dependency, compatibility promise, proof result, or consumer code. It must preserve historical v2 proof lineage while making current-state prose accurately describe the already adopted ORBS v3 consumer boundary.

Consumer: maintainers and agents using Orbit's README, contract index, compatibility history, and crate-decision index to route cross-repository work.

Trigger: read current Orbit documentation after Venus adopted exact Orbit proof `3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174` and reconciled accepted native dogfood at Venus metadata revision `4f799fef1c3e10e86d70b708708f7c2702d7aee8`.

Result: current-state sections say Venus consumes canonical ORBS v3 and distinguish completed protocol adoption, accepted Eon/Eonova native primary-selection dogfood, and the narrower platform/destination gaps that remain.

Important failures: do not rewrite historical v2 proofs as v3, refresh a contract proof merely because docs changed, widen accepted Eon/Eonova primary-selection evidence to unexercised destinations/platforms, or change compatibility policy.

## Why

Orbit's canonical docs still describe Venus as an ORBS v2 consumer awaiting v3 adoption, but the exact Venus manifest already pins the accepted v3 producer and VEN-C13 records partial v3 consumption. The stale prose can misroute integration work and obscure which gap remains open.

Impact: LOW-MED. Effort: S. Risk: LOW. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- `README.md:21-25`: says Venus still consumes v2 until a separate native delivery proof.
- `README.md:219-225`: says v3 remains intentionally incompatible until Venus adopts the exact Orbit revision.
- `docs/CRATES.md:17`: says Venus revision `2d36c72...` still consumes v2.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:37`: ORB-C9 describes a healthy ORBS v2 attachment although current Orbit accepts v3 and v3 retained the selection messages.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:39`: ORB-C11's gap combines Venus native-delivery proof with Eonova acceptance as open.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:115-119`: compatibility history phrases Venus adoption as future.
- Exact accepted Eon `docs/CONTRACTS.md:280-322` and closed `eon-refresh-clipboard-runtimes-0pt` record Eon `0e25ebc2311d7e41edf90c940f8211dd5839bb83`, Eonova `4fda9b67b0faa33561624633229135e5e2d579ea`, Venus `2d3498258920736eb1bdae2b8869b6547b9735d4`, canonical ORBS v3/ORB-C11 consumption, native Wayland primary-selection delivery, detached-write denial, and preserved live processes.
- Closed Venus planning owner `ven-record-ven-c13-native-dogfood-hm0` reconciled that external acceptance evidence into VEN-C13 at Venus `4f799fef1c3e10e86d70b708708f7c2702d7aee8` without changing its source proof or `Partially proved` status.
- Audit `orb-audit-orbit-integration-ur9` independently verified the Eon/Eonova evidence and routed this expanded reconciliation.
- Exact Venus `Cargo.toml:13` at accepted source `4f799fef1c3e10e86d70b708708f7c2702d7aee8` pins Orbit `3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174`.
- Exact Venus `docs/CONTRACTS.md:16,23-26` records partial VEN-C13 canonical v3 consumption and preserves earlier v2 behavior/proofs.
- Audit `orb-audit-orbit-protocols-bkk` recorded the mismatch at Orbit `7d34399b15496513f7f91b94acd32e8d04389e16`.

## Reference classification

Required before editing:

- Current `AGENTS.md`, this complete Bead, Orbit `README.md`, `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, `docs/CRATES.md`, `docs/RATIONALE.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Exact current Venus `Cargo.toml`, lockfile Orbit source, README, reconciled VEN-C13 contract row from `ven-record-ven-c13-native-dogfood-hm0`, and the proof/update history around Orbit `3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174`.
- Exact accepted Eon `docs/CONTRACTS.md:280-322`, closed `eon-refresh-clipboard-runtimes-0pt`, and published Eon/Eonova sources solely for the already accepted downstream evidence.
- Closed `orb-ll1.1` and the protocol audit record to distinguish producer proof, consumer adoption, native dogfood, and runtime acceptance.

Comparison only:

- Historical ORBS v2 contract and proof rows, solely to preserve their exact lineage.

Rejected scope:

- Reproving ORB-C9 or ORB-C11, editing Venus/Eon/Eonova, changing ORBS bytes, or widening the accepted native primary-selection/runtime evidence.

No crate or dependency decision is involved.

## Scope

In scope:

- Current-state prose in `README.md`.
- The canonical consumer row in `docs/CRATES.md`.
- ORB-C9/ORB-C11 current wording and v3 compatibility/update-order prose in `docs/CONTRACTS.md`.
- Any directly duplicate current-state sentence in `docs/RATIONALE.md` only if exact inspection shows it is stale.

Out of scope:

- `CHANGELOG.md` chronological entries that accurately describe the original owner-first sequence at the time.
- Historical v1/v2 proof identities and Venus contract rows that intentionally retain v2 evidence.
- Product code, tests, manifests, lockfiles, proof commits, contract behavior, consumer repositories, and new native dogfood.
- General README rewriting or unrelated documentation cleanup.

## Implementation notes

1. Verify the exact current Venus pin and VEN-C13 status immediately before editing.
2. Change only current-state assertions:
   - Venus consumes exact canonical ORBS v3;
   - the v3 producer proof is `3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174`;
   - VEN-C13 consumption remains partial after accepted Eon/Eonova native primary-selection dogfood because Wayland-without-data-control, macOS, broader-compositor, and unexercised-destination gaps remain;
   - Eon/Eonova runtime acceptance is complete only for the exact recorded artifact and observation.
3. Make ORB-C9's active attachment wording reflect current v3 while retaining its historical proof provenance.
4. Turn the v3 compatibility paragraph into accepted update history: Orbit updated first, Venus adopted the exact revision, no adapter/window exists, and later runtime acceptance remains separately owned.
5. Do not update proof commits or claim `Proved` from this docs-only reconciliation.
6. Preserve concise present-tense current-state language.

Portability disposition: neutral; documentation only.

## Acceptance criteria

1. No current-state Orbit prose says Venus still consumes ORBS v2 or has not adopted the v3 package.
2. README names exact v3 consumption and separates protocol adoption from native delivery/runtime acceptance.
3. `docs/CRATES.md` accurately describes the canonical std-only package and current exact Venus consumer.
4. ORB-C9 names the current session revision without changing its selection contract or historical proof evidence.
5. ORB-C11 and compatibility prose distinguish completed Venus codec/model adoption plus exact accepted Eon/Eonova primary-selection dogfood from the narrower platform/destination gaps that remain.
6. Historical v2 proof rows, commit identities, and chronological changelog statements remain intact.
7. No product contract, proof status, code, test, manifest, dependency, or consumer repository changes.
8. Governance and diff checks pass.

## Verification

- `rg -n 'Venus still consumes v2|still consumes the accepted ORBS v2|intentionally incompatible until|must then adopt' README.md docs` should return no stale current-state assertion.
- `rg -n 'ORBS v2|ORBS v3|3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174|VEN-C13' README.md docs/CONTRACTS.md docs/CRATES.md docs/RATIONALE.md CHANGELOG.md` should show coherent current and historical statements.
- Inspect exact Venus `Cargo.toml`, lockfile, README, and `docs/CONTRACTS.md` at the recorded revision.
- `cargo run --locked --quiet -p orbit-governance -- .` should report `governance: ok`.
- `git diff --check` should exit 0.
- `br lint <this-id>` should report no issue before closure.
- `br sync --flush-only` should persist Beads state.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if Venus no longer pins the accepted Orbit v3 revision.
- Stop if the closed Venus owner record or exact Eon/Eonova evidence can no longer be tied to Venus source proof `2d3498258920736eb1bdae2b8869b6547b9735d4` and accepted metadata revision `4f799fef1c3e10e86d70b708708f7c2702d7aee8`.
- Stop if correcting the text would change, retire, add, or reprove an indexed contract rather than reconcile current facts.
- Stop if another active issue owns the same documentation surfaces.

## Maintenance notes

Do not erase history to make current state simple. Keep historical proof language tied to its revision and reserve present-tense claims for the exact current consumer boundary.

Completed under the user-selected restart-and-redo path with a fresh Execution baseline, a later Reference gate, and current Closure evidence; no protocol exception was used.

title: Recover after transient Linux PTY EIO
description:
## Contract Routing

Hardens ORB-C1 and preserves ORB-C5 plus ORB-C2 through ORB-C4 and ORB-C6 through ORB-C11. It changes neither terminal authority nor ORBF/ORBS bytes.

Consumer: an attached or later reattached local client whose live Orbit PTY child temporarily has no slave descriptor open.

Trigger: Linux reports EIO while reading the PTY master, but Orbit's authoritative direct child has not exited and later reopens its controlling terminal.

Result: Orbit does not irreversibly declare the Session terminal closed from that transient condition; later PTY output and semantic input continue through the same authoritative terminal Session. Confirmed child exit or an independently proved terminal condition still closes the PTY deterministically.

Important failures: no unbounded busy loop, CPU spin, input buffering growth, indefinite false liveness, hidden child-exit delay, duplicate PTY owner, or platform behavior leaked into the neutral owner loop.

Impact: HIGH. Effort: M. Implementation risk: MED. Confidence: HIGH.

## Why

The Linux platform seam maps every PTY-master EIO directly to permanent closure. Linux PTYs can return EIO while all slave descriptors are temporarily closed even though the live child later reopens /dev/tty. Orbit then removes the PTY from polling and rejects later input, violating the live-session behavior ORB-C1 is meant to preserve.

## Evidence

- `src/platform.rs:270-280`: PTY-master EIO maps directly to `PtyIo::Closed`.
- `src/main.rs:396-469`: `Closed` permanently removes the PTY from the poll set.
- `src/main.rs:748-750`: later semantic input is rejected as terminal-closed.
- Closed audit `orb-audit-orbit-platform-t4s`, finding F1, at source `750490f40f348b66aa8809c66c40587ca8db741f`: a real child closed every slave descriptor, retained a regular marker fd, slept, reopened `/dev/tty`, wrote output, and stayed alive. The marker recorded `closed,reopened`; the client received `PTY is closed` and could not observe the reopened terminal.
- The same audit records socat's `sitout-eio` behavior as independent Linux PTY evidence and found no duplicate Bead.
- Current Orbit `7d34399b15496513f7f91b94acd32e8d04389e16` retains the same platform classification.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start Orbit with a child that retains one regular marker fd, closes every PTY slave descriptor, waits, reopens `/dev/tty`, writes a marker, waits for input, then exits.
2. Attach the canonical client before the close and keep the direct child alive throughout the gap.
3. On the audited revision, observe `PtyIo::Closed` / terminal-closed after the master read returns EIO even though the child records `closed,reopened`.
4. Send semantic input after reopen; observe that Orbit has removed the PTY from polling and rejects the input instead of routing it.

Expected: the same live Session observes later output and routes later input. Actual: transient EIO permanently closes Orbit's PTY path.

## Reference Classification

Required before code:

- Current `AGENTS.md`, this complete Bead, ORB-C1/ORB-C5 rows and exact proofs, `docs/REFERENCES.md` platform/lifecycle route, `docs/RATIONALE.md`, `docs/CRATES.md`, current platform owner/callers, and lifecycle tests.
- Exact libc 0.2.189, Linux PTY semantics, and socat EIO evidence recorded by the platform audit.
- Apple PTY EOF/error evidence already routed by `orb-pmp`, only to keep the neutral outcome and macOS replacement credible.

Comparison only:

- Existing child-exit observation and bounded poll scheduling.
- socat's retry control only as behavioral evidence; do not copy its CLI or make a configurable framework.

Rejected scope:

- Reopening or replacing the PTY, emulating slave ownership, polling `/proc`, a new async runtime, a generic portability trait, a dependency, or persistence after Orbit/machine restart.

No Crate gate is required unless evidence contradicts the expected no-dependency shape.

## Scope

In scope:

- The minimum Linux platform outcome/lifecycle state in `src/platform.rs` and existing owner-loop handling in `src/main.rs`.
- One real PTY regression that closes all slave descriptors, reopens `/dev/tty`, emits output, receives later semantic input, and exits.
- Bounded retry/backoff and direct-child exit interaction.
- Contract proof metadata, README LOC, and CHANGELOG only after accepted proof if user-visible behavior changes.

Out of scope:

- Socket claiming, background job-group shutdown, Eon orchestration, protocol bytes, terminal semantics, macOS implementation, new public options, or dependency changes.

## Implementation Notes

1. Record the required execution baseline and reference gate before the first test or product edit.
2. Write the real PTY lifecycle regression first. It must fail on the exact audited EIO closure and retain a direct-child liveness oracle.
3. Choose the smallest platform-owned distinction that treats EIO as transient only while the authoritative lifecycle permits it; keep timing/bounds explicit and avoid spinning.
4. Preserve terminal closure after confirmed child exit and every existing pressure, detach, input, signal, and cleanup invariant.
5. Re-run the complete indexed ORB-C1 and ORB-C5 checks and update proof metadata under the repository proof lifecycle.

Portability disposition: isolated platform dependency. Linux behavior changes inside `src/platform.rs`; the platform-neutral owner sees explicit outcomes. macOS behavior remains unproved.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A live child may close all PTY slave descriptors, reopen `/dev/tty`, emit a marker, receive later semantic input, and exit through the same Orbit Session.
2. No transient EIO alone produces a terminal-closed client failure or permanently removes a live PTY.
3. Confirmed child exit still closes the PTY, drains accepted final output, reaps the child, and removes the socket.
4. Retry work is bounded and produces no measurable idle spin or unbounded input/output storage.
5. Detach/reattach, slow-client pressure, resize, terminal replies, and shutdown behavior remain green.
6. ORB-C1 is hardened, ORB-C5 is preserved, and unchanged contracts/protocol bytes retain their owners.
7. No dependency, public flag, generic portability framework, PTY replacement, or second authority is added.
8. README LOC, contract proof lifecycle, CHANGELOG if applicable, governance, and canonical checks are current.

## Verification

- Add one real PTY lifecycle test reproducing close/reopen and proving later output plus input.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo check --locked --workspace`
- `cargo test --locked --workspace`
- `cargo run --locked --quiet -p orbit-governance -- .`
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`
- `br lint <this-id>`
- `br sync --flush-only`

All commands should exit 0; the regression must fail on the audited revision and pass on the candidate.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if current Linux evidence no longer reproduces or direct-child exit cannot distinguish the terminal state without a new contract.
- Stop if the implementation needs a dependency, public setting, new protocol, platform framework, or behavior outside ORB-C1/ORB-C5.
- Stop if another active issue owns `src/platform.rs`, the PTY-read lifecycle branch, or the same proof surface.
- Stop rather than weakening shutdown, data-loss protection, or trust-boundary validation.

## Maintenance Notes

Do not turn one Linux retry condition into a general PTY recovery subsystem. Retain the existing direct child as liveness authority and add only the minimum bounded state the regression proves necessary.
notes: Accepted owner and shape: src/platform.rs remains the single Linux PTY I/O policy owner. Read-side EIO retries after one fixed 10 ms sleep only while Orbit retains the authoritative direct Child; after reaping it is Closed, and write-side EIO remains Closed. Rejected immediate retry because it measured 100/100 CPU ticks; rejected a deadline/poll-suppression state machine, new outcome, dependency, configuration, PTY replacement, and portability framework as unnecessary. Proof cb0703010c3a4944980404b665abff795be09fb4 passed the 59-test locked suite, formatting, check, governance, Clippy, diff, focused 20/20 native stress, ORBIT_MEMCHECK-shaped functional run, and exact ORB-C10 terminfo/real-PTY preservation checks. No dependency or protocol changed. Product Rust source/tests: 8,064 lines. Portability: isolated Linux platform dependency; macOS and restart persistence remain unproved/out of scope.

title: Serialize stale Orbit socket claims
description:
## Contract Routing

Hardens ORB-C1 and the local Unix-socket trust boundary while preserving ORB-C2 through ORB-C11. It changes neither the socket path contract, one-client attachment rule, ORBF/ORBS bytes, nor Eon/Venus behavior.

Consumer: a local launcher starting Orbit at one configured socket path after a stale socket inode remains.

Trigger: two Orbit processes concurrently attempt to claim the same stale Unix socket.

Result: exactly one live Orbit owner becomes reachable at the path; every loser fails cleanly without unlinking or replacing the winner's endpoint. Cleanup remains identity-guarded.

Important failures: no two live owners, unreachable winning process, symlink/path substitution, deletion of a live endpoint, unbounded retry, global lock, new daemon, or weaker permissions.

Impact: HIGH. Effort: M. Implementation risk: MED. Confidence: HIGH.

## Why

`create_listener` checks one inode, attempts a connection, then unconditionally removes the current path before bind. Two contenders can both decide the original inode is stale; one can unlink the other's newly bound socket and bind again, leaving two live Orbit processes with only one reachable.

## Evidence

- `src/platform.rs:202-227`: stale-path inspection, connection attempt, unconditional removal, and bind are not one serialized/identity-checked claim.
- The existing `SocketGuard` protects final cleanup identity, but not concurrent stale replacement.
- Closed audit `orb-audit-orbit-platform-t4s`, finding F2, at source `750490f40f348b66aa8809c66c40587ca8db741f`: starting two current Orbit processes from one deliberately stale socket left both alive on stress iteration 17 (PIDs 346627 and 346628); one had unlinked the other's replacement and rebound the path.
- The audit terminated both processes, confirmed no survivor, and found no duplicate Bead.
- Current Orbit `7d34399b15496513f7f91b94acd32e8d04389e16` retains the same claim sequence.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Bind and close a Unix listener while leaving its stale socket inode at the configured Orbit path.
2. Release two Orbit processes simultaneously against that same path and wait for startup convergence.
3. Repeat with bounded cleanup until the audited race is exercised.
4. On the audited revision, observe two live Orbit processes: one contender removed the other's replacement socket and rebound the path, leaving only one process reachable.

Expected: exactly one live reachable owner and one bounded loser. Actual: two live owners can remain, with one unreachable.

## Reference Classification

Required before code:

- Current `AGENTS.md`, this complete Bead, ORB-C1 row/proof, `docs/REFERENCES.md` platform route, `docs/RATIONALE.md`, `docs/CRATES.md`, current `create_listener`/SocketGuard owner, startup tests, and exact socket permission/path policy.
- Exact libc 0.2.189 and Linux Unix-domain socket/path semantics used by the existing seam.
- Existing Orbit socket-identity and simultaneous-attach evidence, only for invariants they already prove.

Comparison only:

- Standard-library/native filesystem and socket primitives capable of making the claim exclusive or identity-checked.
- Existing lock/claim patterns already in the repositories if exact inspection finds one.

Rejected scope:

- Caller retries as the owner, a global product lock, a lock service/daemon, PID files, process-name scans, branch-dependent behavior, remote transport, a new dependency, or changing the socket path/public protocol.

No Crate gate is required unless the standard library/native platform cannot express the selected claim safely.

## Scope

In scope:

- The minimum stale-socket claim logic and focused helpers in `src/platform.rs`.
- One deterministic or bounded stress regression starting simultaneous contenders from one stale inode and proving exactly one live reachable owner.
- Identity-preserving cleanup, permissions, symlink/path defenses, and startup failure behavior.
- Contract proof metadata, README LOC, and CHANGELOG only after accepted proof if user-visible behavior changes.

Out of scope:

- PTY I/O/EIO, process-group shutdown, Eon launch convergence, remote sockets, multiple active clients, public locks/options, portability framework, or dependency changes.

## Implementation Notes

1. Record the execution baseline and reference gate before the first test or product edit.
2. Write the simultaneous stale-claim regression first, with exact process cleanup even on failure.
3. Choose the first sufficient platform-owned claim using existing standard-library/native primitives. The loser must fail; it must never retry by unlinking an unverified current path.
4. Preserve current live-socket rejection, endpoint permissions, non-socket/path defenses, and SocketGuard cleanup identity.
5. Run the indexed ORB-C1 lifecycle checks and update proof metadata through the accepted proof lifecycle.

Portability disposition: isolated platform dependency. The claim remains behind the existing socket platform seam; macOS implementation/behavior remains unproved.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. From one stale socket inode, simultaneous Orbit starts leave exactly one live process reachable at the configured path.
2. Every losing process exits with a bounded explicit startup failure and cannot unlink or replace the winner.
3. A genuinely live socket is never removed; a genuinely stale socket remains replaceable.
4. Non-socket paths, symlink/path substitution, permissions, and identity-guarded final cleanup remain fail-closed.
5. Repetition sufficient to exercise the former race produces no two-owner or unreachable-owner result and leaves no process/socket residue.
6. ORB-C1 is hardened without changing one-client attachment, socket path, ORBF/ORBS, dependencies, or callers.
7. README LOC, proof metadata, governance, and canonical checks are current.

## Verification

- Add a focused simultaneous stale-socket claim regression with bounded repetitions and guaranteed process cleanup.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo check --locked --workspace`
- `cargo test --locked --workspace`
- `cargo run --locked --quiet -p orbit-governance -- .`
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`
- `br lint <this-id>`
- `br sync --flush-only`

All commands should exit 0; the focused test must fail against the audited race and pass on the candidate.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the race no longer reproduces or current path/permission ownership differs materially.
- Stop if correctness requires a daemon, dependency, public lock/configuration, Eon change, or new cross-repository contract.
- Stop if another active issue owns `create_listener`, socket startup, or the same lifecycle proof.
- Stop rather than weakening live-owner detection, permissions, or path-substitution defenses.

## Maintenance Notes

Fix the claim once at the socket owner. Do not add launch retries in Eon or duplicate endpoint arbitration in callers.

description:
## Contract routing

This is repository-governance tooling only. It changes no ORB product contract, runtime behavior, proof revision, wire format, portability promise, dependency choice, or CI topology.

Consumer: Orbit maintainers and CI running `orbit-governance` against canonical repository metadata.

Trigger: the governance command reads `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, `docs/CRATES.md`, and `.beads/issues.jsonl` after repository policy or planning data changes.

Result: deterministic Orbit-specific metadata defects still fail, while the tool no longer classifies implementation work or interprets execution, reference, closure, portability, crate, or protocol-exception prose owned by `AGENTS.md` and applicability-aware review.

Important failures: do not remove unique contract or crate safeguards; do not replace them with shell parsing; do not keep duplicate tracker validation; do not claim that structural checks prove process compliance; do not change Cargo manifests, dependencies, CI, product contracts, or runtime code.

## Accepted decision and evidence

title: Prevent stale client readiness from panicking Orbit
description:
## Observable contract

Consumer: the one attached local ORBS client and the live PTY session.

Trigger: poll reports both PTY and client readiness, then processing PTY output disconnects the client because clipboard-effect or presentation output cannot be admitted.

Result: Orbit treats the stale client-ready bit as obsolete, continues authoritative PTY/session ownership, and accepts a later client. It never unwraps a client that an earlier action in the same poll turn removed.

Important failures: do not skip a still-live ready client, reorder PTY-before-client processing, retain failed client storage, add a second client state owner, or weaken queue bounds.

## Contract routing

title: Upstream erased-row loss for libghostty tracked references
description:
Low-priority external correctness work in Ghostty. This Bead changes no product contract, does not block orb-j0m, and must not create an Orbit fork or private adapter.

Known failure:
External tracked grid references can silently change semantic identity after erased scrollback is removed. CSI 3 J reaches PageList history erasure; affected pins are remapped to retained storage rather than marked garbage. Later output can move the replacement cell into history, allowing an old external reference to resolve to the wrong row.

Outcome:
Confirm the failure against current Ghostty main, obtain the required human contribution access, and propose the smallest upstream correction if maintainers accept the issue. The native Orbit viewport and selection design does not expose long-lived history references, so this work is independent maintenance rather than product-path work.
design:

- Internal viewport and selection pins retained existing remapping behavior, Pin remained 16 bytes, and focused tracked-grid-reference tests passed.
- No public C API, Rust wrapper, dependency, or Orbit change was required.

title: Validate canonical ORBF cell-width topology
description:
## Contract routing

Hardens existing `ORB-C4` and `ORB-C6` and preserves `ORB-C3`, `ORB-C5`, and `ORB-C7` through `ORB-C11`; it adds no product capability and does not authorize a new ORBF/ORBS wire revision. The canonical `orbit-protocol` frame validator remains the sole owner of accepted ORBF v1 cell-width topology.

The preceding shared-validator hardening `orb-harden-orbf-capabilities-6v9` closed at accepted proof `6de95296d252c119d4fdba2d9b03cec1a09355ae`. This Bead starts from that immutable ORB-C4/C6 owner revision; the historical Venus audit used package `3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174`, and Venus must consume the resulting owner-first proof separately.

## Why

Consumers: Orbit's authoritative presentation producer and every canonical ORBF v1 decoder/reducer, including Venus.

Trigger: code encodes, decodes, or directly reduces a complete ORBF v1 frame containing `Wide`, `SpacerTail`, or `SpacerHead` roles.

Result: the canonical owner accepts only width-role layouts that preserve the selected libghostty terminal-grid topology. At minimum, ordinary wide cells and their tails must be contiguous and correctly ordered, spacer tails cannot be orphaned, and wrapped spacer heads must occur only in the exact edge/wrap sequence selected by the accepted producer. Invalid topology fails before a reducer or consumer materializes it.

Important failures: no partial frame acceptance, no silent normalization, no Venus compensating validator, and no over-restrictive rule inferred without checking exact libghostty wrap/viewport semantics.

Venus audit `ven-audit-venus-scene-renderer-2db` found the gap at Venus `4f799fef1c3e10e86d70b708708f7c2702d7aee8`. Impact MED. Effort S-M. Implementation risk MED because validation hardening and exact consumer pins/proofs must advance. Confidence HIGH in the canonical gap; confidence LOW that the accepted producer emits an invalid topology.

## Evidence

- `crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:223-239`: ORBF exposes four cell-width roles.
- `crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:553-582` at accepted proof `6de95296...`: `validate_frame` checks capabilities, dimensions, row/cell counts, cursor bounds, and encoded size, but not width-role topology.
- `crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:643-659`: raw decode validates only the width tag, so any ordering of valid tags is canonical.
- `crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:972-1039`: the rich codec fixture itself arranges `Wide` at a row end, `SpacerTail` at the next row start, and `SpacerHead` afterward; it proves tags/round-trip, not a producer-valid grid.
- `src/presentation.rs:110-155,194-200`: the accepted producer maps exact libghostty width roles directly into the canonical frame.
- Pinned Ghostty `a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083` `src/terminal/page.zig:510-555`: page integrity requires a SpacerTail to follow Wide and requires SpacerHead at the last column of a wrapped row.
- The same Ghostty source `src/terminal/Terminal.zig:1187-1220`: an ordinary wide character emits Wide followed by SpacerTail; wrapping at the real edge first emits SpacerHead, then wraps and emits the wide pair.
- Venus `src/scene.rs:435-535` at `4f799fef...`: Scene documents a validated-frame precondition, treats Wide as spanning two columns, and skips spacer roles. Adjacent Wide heads or a missing tail can therefore omit content; a maximal malformed run can overflow debug arithmetic.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Starting from an otherwise valid ORBF v1 frame, replace one row with adjacent `Wide` cells, a `Wide` not followed by `SpacerTail`, or an orphan `SpacerTail`.
2. Call canonical frame encoding; observe success because `validate_frame` checks no role adjacency.
3. Mutate valid encoded cell-width tag bytes into the same malformed ordering; observe canonical decode success.
4. Push the typed frame directly into `FrameReducer`; observe acceptance when its revision is newer.
5. Project the canonical-valid result through the exact Venus Scene consumer and observe skipped columns or invalid run arithmetic.

Expected: the canonical owner rejects producer-invalid width topology before reducer/consumer acceptance. Actual: valid individual tags are unconstrained.

## Reference classification

Required before code:
- Current `AGENTS.md`, this complete Bead, closed predecessor `orb-harden-orbf-capabilities-6v9` and accepted proof `6de95296d252c119d4fdba2d9b03cec1a09355ae`, `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, `docs/REFERENCES.md`, `docs/RATIONALE.md`, and `docs/CRATES.md`.
- Exact accepted `ORB-C4`/`ORB-C6` proof and canonical `orbit-protocol` source at the execution baseline.
- Exact libghostty-vt/libghostty-vt-sys 0.2.1 and pinned Ghostty `a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083`: public `CellWide`, RenderState row/cell iteration, page integrity, wide printing, wrap, resize/reflow, and viewport-boundary behavior.
- Exact current Orbit producer and every canonical frame fixture/reducer caller.
- Exact Venus consumer revision and Scene width-role interpretation, only to prove the independently released boundary and required consumer update order.

Conditional:
- A focused real-libghostty corpus for viewport top/bottom boundaries, resizing, or reflow if source semantics do not uniquely determine whether a cross-row SpacerHead sequence may be truncated at a complete-frame boundary.

Comparison-only:
- No second terminal implementation is required unless exact selected libghostty behavior remains ambiguous after the focused corpus.

Rejected:
- Per-consumer validation, normalization/repair, a second schema, a new error framework, dependency, general grid validator framework, or new wire revision.

No Crate gate is expected. Platform disposition: neutral.

## Scope

In scope:
- `crates/protocol/src/lib.rs` existing frame validation and the fewest strong co-located encoder/raw-decoder/direct-reducer tests.
- Correction of existing protocol fixtures that are contract-invalid once exact topology is established.
- `src/presentation.rs` only if a focused producer check is required to prove emitted topology, not to normalize it.
- `README.md` LOC scorecard and `docs/CONTRACTS.md` proof lifecycle metadata.
- Exact cross-repository compatibility classification and owner-first/consumer-second update order.

Out of scope:
- Editing Venus in this Bead, changing public width variants/tags, new frame/session revision, compatibility adapter/window, graphics, shaping, grapheme-width calculation, terminal repair, dependency, or broader codec cleanup.

## Implementation notes

1. Rebaseline the exact accepted validator at `6de95296d252c119d4fdba2d9b03cec1a09355ae` and rerun duplicate and consumer searches.
2. Use TDD: require encoder, raw decoder, and direct reducer rejection plus non-mutation of an already accepted reducer frame.
3. Derive the smallest exact topology rules from selected libghostty, including ordinary same-row pairs and wrapped SpacerHead sequences; do not guess across viewport boundaries.
4. Put the invariant in the existing shared frame-validation owner so encode, decode, and reducer cannot drift. Reject rather than coerce.
5. Correct only fixtures proven invalid; retain accepted producer bytes byte-for-byte for valid frames.
6. Classify this as compatible hardening of contract-invalid ORBF v1 bytes only if every accepted producer and known consumer agrees. Otherwise stop for the user's breaking-change decision.
7. Commit/verify the Orbit source candidate first, then update proof metadata and close. A separate Venus Bead adopts the exact accepted Orbit proof and reruns consumer proofs; no compatibility window.

## Acceptance criteria

- Encoder, raw decoder, and direct reducer reject every locally malformed Wide/SpacerTail pair and every invalid SpacerHead placement selected by the exact producer contract.
- A rejected newer typed frame cannot replace the reducer's prior valid current frame.
- Focused valid cases cover narrow cells, ordinary wide pairs, a real wrapped SpacerHead sequence, relevant viewport boundaries, and producer-derived resize/reflow cases.
- Accepted Orbit producer frames remain byte-for-byte unchanged and pass the canonical validator.
- Venus needs no compensating validator or schema mirror.
- The change is explicitly classified compatible or stopped for a user compatibility decision; known consumers and owner-first update order are recorded.
- No direct dependency, new protocol version, adapter, or compatibility window is introduced.
- ORB-C4/ORB-C6 and every touched proof row are current at closure.

## Verification

- `cargo test --locked -p orbit-protocol` must pass focused width-topology, canonical codec, and reducer checks.
- Run the cheapest focused `src/presentation.rs` producer corpus selected at the Reference gate.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo check --locked --workspace`
- `cargo test --locked --workspace`
- `cargo run --locked --quiet -p orbit-governance -- .`
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`
- `br lint <this-id>`

All commands must exit 0 on one materially unchanged candidate; record exact test counts and environment.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if selected libghostty permits a topology that cannot be validated from one complete ORBF frame without an additional producer field or changed wire semantics.
- Stop if an accepted producer or consumer relies on the malformed layouts; ask the user to choose compatibility/versioning.
- Stop before a new dependency, wire revision, adapter, compatibility window, cross-repository edit, or second validator.
- Stop if another active issue owns canonical frame validation.

## Maintenance notes

The canonical protocol owns trust-boundary topology; Orbit owns producer truth; Venus consumes validated roles. Keep the correction one shared validator plus few strong cases, not a grid framework.

Complete-frame and standalone-row encoding, raw row decoding, and direct FrameReducer admission all call it. title: Record VT and Unicode baselines through Orbit and Venus
description:
Cross-repository verification task with no new user-visible behavior, terminal compatibility promise, or product contract. After orb-bi4.6 proves the first composed dogfood path, record one reproducible VT and Unicode baseline through the actual pinned Orbit server, PTY child, ORBS and ORBF bridge, and Venus native renderer.

Use a focused VTTEST scorecard plus ucs-detect and ucs-browser. The purpose is not to re-prove the complete libghostty terminal engine. It is to detect whether terminal modes, replies, input, structured presentation, Unicode cell semantics, glyph shaping, and native rendering survive the boundaries Eon owns.

Contract routing:
- Changes no EON-C, ORB-C, or VEN-C contract or proof status by itself.
- Exercises the exact accepted ORB-C2 and ORB-C4 through ORB-C6 boundary, later accepted history and selection contracts where relevant, and VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 plus VEN-C7 when accepted. Reconfirm IDs and exact proofs at activation.
- Routes every discrepancy to one Orbit, Venus, Eon, upstream, tool-expectation, or unsupported-capability owner. It repairs none of them.

Out of scope:
- An Eon terminal-emulation profile, xterm compatibility guarantee, exhaustive conformance claim, copied or vendored external suite, esctest integration, upstream libghostty testing, automated screenshot farm, per-push or scheduled CI, product code, protocol changes, new runtime dependencies, performance benchmarking, macOS support, or feature expansion.
design:
Verification plan:

1. Start only after orb-bi4.6 closes with exact accepted Eon, Orbit, and Venus revisions and a reproducible composed launch path. Record a planning and evidence baseline; this is a no-code acceptance run unless a minimum local command is later approved as necessary.
2. Pass a Reference and tool gate before tracked test, script, workflow, Nix, fixture, or documentation edits. Required evidence: the exact VTTEST source and release, applicable DEC manuals and xterm control-sequence documentation, the exact ucs-detect and ucs-browser release with its wcwidth and Unicode data identities, exact pinned libghostty and Ghostty behavior, and the accepted Orbit and Venus contracts. Compare focused direct use, esctest, owned synthetic cases, and no external suite. Keep esctest rejected unless a later exact review shows a maintained profile that removes rather than adds expectation ownership.
3. Launch the exact accepted pair through the existing Eon dogfood path. VTTEST and ucs-detect must run as real PTY children owned by Orbit while the real Venus client renders and supplies input. Do not substitute standalone Ghostty, a fake frame source, the diagnostic text client, raw PTY replay, or a handwritten protocol consumer.
4. Select the smallest VTTEST menu set that crosses owned boundaries: cursor movement and save or restore, margins and scrolling regions, erase behavior, SGR and colors, origin and wrap modes, alternate screen where covered, device status and attributes, resize-sensitive behavior, and representative keyboard sequences. Record pass, deviation, unsupported, ambiguous, and not-run outcomes; never report a blanket conformance score.
5. Run ucs-detect with a saved machine-readable report for bounded representative wide, zero-width, combining, grapheme, emoji ZWJ, variation-selector, regional-indicator, and language cases. Run ucs-browser visually for alignment and glyph quality using the actual Venus font stack. Distinguish Orbit and libghostty cursor-position or cell-width semantics from Venus shaping, fallback, atlas, and visual alignment.
6. Treat the ucs-detect wcwidth model as one comparator rather than product law. Classify every delta against the exact Unicode versions, accepted libghostty behavior, advertised terminal modes, actual glyph result, and prior Eon baseline. Unsupported graphics or terminal modes are not failures merely because a probe exists.
7. During a focused stateful case, resize once and detach then reattach Venus once to check that the observed state remains coherent across the accepted bridge. Do not repeat the broader lifecycle and application matrix already proved by orb-bi4.6.
8. Record exact Eon manifest and component commits; operating system, display backend, GPU and driver, locale, TERM and capability declarations, geometry, font and fallback stack; tool and Unicode versions; commands, menu items, generated report hashes or locations, screenshots where needed, elapsed time, and every classified result.
9. A regression in a claimed supported capability or an Orbit to Venus boundary invariant blocks closure and names one owner. A tool expectation mismatch or unsupported feature remains recorded evidence. Product fixes, protocol changes, renderer changes, new capabilities, and upstream work require separately authorized owner Beads.
10. The initial baseline is manual Linux evidence. Rerun after relevant libghostty, Unicode, font, shaping, input, presentation, or renderer changes and before releases carrying them. A future accepted macOS client consumes the method in its own platform proof rather than inheriting this Linux result.

Do not add a CHANGELOG entry. README LOC changes only if tracked handwritten verification text is later required; generated logs and screenshots remain evidence artifacts, not product source.
acceptance_criteria:
1. orb-bi4.6 is closed with exact accepted Eon, Orbit, and Venus revisions, and the baseline records the EON-C, ORB-C, and VEN-C implementations exercised without changing or promoting any contract.
2. A pre-edit Reference and tool gate records exact VTTEST, DEC or xterm references, ucs-detect, wcwidth, Unicode data, libghostty, Ghostty, Eon, Orbit, and Venus identities and licenses. It compares direct focused use with esctest, owned synthetic checks, and no external suite.
3. VTTEST and ucs-detect run inside the real Orbit-owned PTY while the real pinned Venus client renders and sends input through canonical ORBS and ORBF. Evidence identifies the actual processes and rejects standalone-emulator or fake-frame substitution.
4. One focused VTTEST scorecard covers the selected cursor, scrolling-region, erase, style or color, origin or wrap, terminal-reply, resize, and keyboard surfaces. Every item is classified as pass, deviation, unsupported, ambiguous, or not run with no blanket xterm or DEC conformance claim.
5. One saved ucs-detect report covers bounded representative width, combining, grapheme, emoji ZWJ, variation-selector, regional-indicator, and language cases. One ucs-browser pass visually checks alignment, shaping, fallback, and glyph quality in Venus.
6. Results distinguish authoritative Orbit and libghostty state, replies, and cell semantics from Venus presentation, shaping, fallback, and visual rendering. No client-side terminal model or alternate expectation owner is introduced.
7. One selected stateful result remains coherent across a real resize and Venus detach and reattach. This does not duplicate or replace the orb-bi4.6 application and lifecycle matrix.
8. Every deviation names one exact owner: Orbit, Venus, Eon composition, pinned upstream, external-suite expectation, environment, or explicitly unsupported capability. A regression in accepted behavior blocks closure; no product repair occurs in this Bead.
9. Evidence records exact commits, tools, platform, display, GPU, locale, TERM, geometry, fonts, Unicode data, commands, selected cases, report or screenshot locations, duration, and classified outcomes so a later run can compare deltas.
10. No external test source is copied or vendored; no esctest profile, compatibility layer, runtime dependency, product mode, protocol surface, CI job, schedule, screenshot farm, or full upstream conformance suite is added.
11. The recurring trigger is recorded as after relevant engine, Unicode, shaping, input, presentation, renderer, or platform changes and before releases that carry them. Linux evidence makes no macOS claim.
12. Any tracked planning or minimal verification surface passes governance and git diff checks. Closure records limitations and one result: accepted integration baseline, or held open with one named owner regression.

User decision on 2026-08-07: periodically exercise the real composed stack with focused VTTEST plus ucs-detect and ucs-browser rather than owning a duplicate Ghostty conformance profile. This cross-repository acceptance Bead changes and repairs no product contract.

The automated and native Linux baseline is durable in comments 478 and 479. Comment 479 supersedes only the mistaken ucs-browser visual-pass statement in comment 478; all other quantitative and lifecycle evidence remains valid. Two independent accepted-boundary regressions block closure:

Do not repeat unrelated VTTEST menus or ucs-detect coverage unless a changed owner invalidates them. Native window-only captures and machine delimiter checks remove the need for human testing or desktop focus.

Recommended sequence: Venus owner fix, Orbit/libghostty owner fix and crate decision, Eon composition refresh, then this acceptance closure. Expected remaining acceptance risk after those prerequisites: low.

Correction to comment 478

Reinspection shows that the earlier Xvfb wide, grapheme, and ZWJ captures already contain delimiter drift and expanded component glyphs. The quantitative ucs-detect and VTTEST results in comment 478 are unchanged.
- The first native grapheme and ZWJ launches omitted mode 2027 and therefore reproduced the known legacy-width control. The grapheme view was rerun with `CSI ?2027h`; its delimiters still failed. The wide single-codepoint page is not repaired by mode 2027 and also failed.

Human observation
- The user reported misaligned cell delimiters on the native wide page, the native legacy grapheme page, the native legacy ZWJ page, and the corrected native mode-2027 grapheme page.
- Human wide screenshot `/tmp/codex-clipboard-rdhi2c.png`, SHA-256 `0bb62a32b5e3fd8a3efa758a3af0ab2aea4e9fe78a906e01573c54a2f7ba3663`, shows both glyph fallback or clipping and shifted delimiters.
- Human legacy-grapheme screenshot `/tmp/codex-clipboard-VMAbDO.png`, SHA-256 `24a0cf754b96f07d31a94b3be6c0788ab6327555bbe2da1a16f514f840626b1d`, shows delimiter drift. The user correctly clarified that glyph outlines may be narrower but the cell delimiters themselves are not collinear.

Independent native capture
- No further human inspection is required. A unique OSC title identified only the isolated Venus Wayland toplevel through `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1`; `grim -T IDENTIFIER` captured only that window, not the desktop or any other application. All captures used the accepted installed Eon, Orbit, and Venus composition and explicit mode 2027.
- Mode-2027 grapheme capture `native-self-graphemes-mode2027.png`, 957x1040, SHA-256 `d27613fea084a19df75dd48946e05464b9157810acddf4aa41d3185b3f706703`.
- Mode-2027 wide capture `native-self-wide2-mode2027.png`, 957x1040, SHA-256 `891df2c0d22af37d1ffeadbeb3b2fd7c903a8318b5d514fd2d35b2fc47b0c777`.
- Mode-2027 ZWJ capture `native-self-zwj-mode2027.png`, 957x1040, SHA-256 `64cff66ab486fbd84b92df9f307e05ef11a1bb4f66d1a39c102000b78aac18bf`.
- All three independently reproduce the failure. Wide and grapheme closing delimiters shift after affected glyphs. The ZWJ page is substantially broken: many sequences expand into component glyphs and displace later delimiters.
- A thresholded ImageMagick connected-component check makes the visual result machine-inspectable. In the 920-pixel content crop, the first delimiter at x=206 remains connected for 891 pixels. Grapheme delimiter pairs expected near x=426/446, x=646/666, and x=866/886 remain connected for only 648 to 666 pixels, then fragment or reappear at shifted x coordinates including 433, 452, 658, 673, 884, and 911. Wide delimiters similarly jump from the nominal pairs to 233, 433, 459, 659, 685, 885, and 911. On the ZWJ page only x=206 remains full-height; later delimiter components fragment into repeated 54- to 72-pixel spans at x=299, 499, 591, 791, and 884. This detects delimiter topology rather than judging glyph outline width.

Exact owner
- Orbit `src/presentation.rs::Extractor::frame` serializes every libghostty RenderState cell independently with its authoritative `CellWidth` and complete `graphemes_utf8` payload. The mode-2027 ucs-detect run measured RI flags and ZWJ at 100%, proving that the authoritative terminal cursor and cell-width semantics are coherent for those selected cases.
- Installed Venus `7fc7e4ba97aaf48b586002934a580ef2d1c31694` loses that placement constraint in `src/scene.rs::Scene::build_glyph_runs`: adjacent same-style cells are concatenated into one `GlyphRun.text` with only a starting column and aggregate column count. `src/render.rs::Renderer::push_cell_text` then sends the whole concatenated run through one cosmic-text or glyphon shaped buffer. Box delimiters and ordinary text are layered, but individual authoritative cell offsets are not supplied. Fallback, complex shaping, bidi, and ZWJ advances can therefore reposition later cell glyphs and delimiters. The current Venus edge source is unchanged on these surfaces relative to the installed proof commit.
- Exact owner: the Eon Desktop Venus renderer and proved `VEN-C1` native materialization contract. This is not owned by Orbit protocol, ucs-browser, the font environment, Xvfb, Wayland, or mode negotiation. A Venus owner Bead must retain per-cell positioning while allowing shaping within each authoritative grapheme or another equivalently constrained shape, then rerun the focused ucs-browser pages on native Wayland and Xvfb.
- The separate DECSCNM failure from comment 478 remains owned by the pinned upstream libghostty StreamTerminal adapter and affects the ORB-C6 extraction path. This Bead is held open on two independent named regressions and repairs neither one.

All isolated human-test and self-capture generations were stopped through their own supervisor. Existing user sessions were untouched.
